words.tr: adj. 溢于言表的；感情奔放的
words.ex: She was effusive in her praise for the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她对老师的赞美非常热情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as effusive, you mean that they express pleasure, gratitude, or approval in a very enthusiastic way.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He dissembles when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会假装。
words.en: To dissemble means to conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.

words.ex: His answer was apt for the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答对这个问题很恰当。
words.en: If someone is apt to do something, they often do it and so it is likely that they will do it again.

words.tr:
v. 皱起；使起褶子；撅起
n. 皱纹；褶子
words.ex: He pucker his lips when he tastes sour lemon.
words.ex_cn: 他尝到酸柠檬时皱起了嘴唇。
words.en: To pucker means to tightly gather or contract into wrinkles or small folds.

words.ex: The ship docked at the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船停靠在海港。
words.en: A harbor is a place on the coast where ships may moor in shelter, especially one protected from rough water by piers, jetties, and other artificial structures.

words.tr:
n. 塑料；
adj. 塑料的；
words.ex: The bottle is made of plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这个瓶子是塑料做的。
words.en: A plastic is a material which is produced from oil by a chemical process and which is used to make many objects. It is light in weight and does not break easily.

words.tr: v. 神化；把…奉若神明；崇拜
words.ex: They deify their ancient heroes.
words.ex_cn: 他们崇拜自己的古代英雄。
words.en: To treat someone or something as a god or goddess, or to consider them as if they were divine.

words.tr:
n. 蔑视
v. 蔑视
words.ex: He looked at the lie with scorn.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you scorn someone or something, you feel or show contempt for them.

words.ex: He was absent from school yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天缺席了学校。
words.en: If someone or something is absent from a place or situation where they should be or where they usually are, they are not there.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.tr:
v. 为 ... 上脚镣；束缚；限制
n. 脚镣；桎梏；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner was fettered with chains.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯被锁链束缚着。
words.en: A fetter is a chain or shackle for the feet, or something that confines or restrains.

words.tr: v. 使变色；弄脏；贬损；伤害名誉
words.ex: He distains all forms of flattery and insincerity.
words.ex_cn: 他蔑视所有形式的奉承和虚伪。
words.en: To regard or treat with contempt; to scorn.

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: The audience gave applause after the song.
words.ex_cn: 歌曲结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: Applause is the noise made by a group of people clapping their hands to show approval or enjoyment.

words.tr: v. 逐渐变细；逐渐减少；
words.ex: The candle tapers toward the top.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛向顶部逐渐变细。
words.en: A taper is a long thin candle or a gradual decrease in width or thickness.

words.ex: He was a gawky teenager with long, awkward limbs.
words.ex_cn: 他是个笨拙的少年，四肢又长又笨拙。
words.en: If you describe someone as gawky, you mean they are awkward and clumsy, often because they are young and have not yet grown into their body.

words.tr: v. 使变质；损害；使失效
words.ex: The poison vitiated the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒物使水源变质。
words.en: To vitiate something means to impair or reduce the quality, value, or effectiveness of it.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr: adj. 无可争辩的；攻不破的；不容置疑的
words.ex: His alibi is unassailable.
words.ex_cn: 他的不在场证明是无可置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something such as a person's reputation or an argument as unassailable, you mean that it cannot be criticized or attacked because it is completely right or true.

words.tr:
v. 同意；赞成
n. 同意；赞成
words.ex: He gave his assent to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了这个计划。
words.en: If you assent to something, you agree to it or agree with it.

words.ex: The dog gave a small nip to his leg.
words.ex_cn: 狗轻轻咬了他的腿一口。
words.en: To nip means to pinch, squeeze, or bite something quickly and sharply. It can also refer to taking a small amount of a drink.

words.ex: He is timorous when speaking in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前说话时很胆怯。
words.en: If you describe someone as timorous, you mean that they are nervous and lack courage or confidence.

words.tr:
v. 补充；
n. 补充物；附加费；
words.ex: He supplements his income by teaching part-time.
words.ex_cn: 他通过兼职教学来补充收入。
words.en: A supplement is something that is added to something else in order to make it complete or better.

words.tr:
v. 争论；争执；吵架
n. 争吵；口角
words.ex: They wrangle over the price every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为价格争执。
words.en: If you wrangle with someone, you argue with them in a noisy or angry way.

words.ex: The bustle of the market filled the morning air.
words.ex_cn: 市场的喧哗充满了早晨的空气。
words.en: If someone bustles somewhere, they move there in a hurried way, often because they are very busy or excited.

words.tr: v. （清楚地）发音；清楚地表明；阐明
words.ex: He tries to enunciate each word clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他努力清晰地发出每个单词的音。
words.en: To enunciate means to pronounce words clearly and distinctly, or to state something clearly and in detail.

words.tr: n. 赞美诗；合唱队；众赞歌
words.ex: The church choir performed a beautiful chorale during the service.
words.ex_cn: 教堂合唱团在礼拜中演唱了一首美丽的赞美诗。
words.en: A chorale is a musical composition (or part of one) consisting of or resembling a harmonized version of a simple, stately hymn tune.

words.ex: The old building will implode if the explosives go off.
words.ex_cn: 如果炸药引爆，这座旧楼会坍塌。
words.en: If something implodes, it collapses into itself in a sudden and violent way.

words.ex: The city's sprawl has covered many farmlands.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的杂乱无序的拓展覆盖了许多农田。
words.en: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.

words.ex: He tries to rive the wood with an axe.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用斧头劈开木头。
words.en: To tear or split apart violently.

words.ex: The long wait disgruntles the customers.
words.ex_cn: 漫长的等待让顾客感到不满。
words.en: If you are disgruntled, you are angry or dissatisfied because something has not happened the way you wanted.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
n. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
words.ex: He mutters under his breath when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 当他生气时，他会低声嘟囔。
words.en: To speak or say something in a low voice that is hard to hear, often because you are annoyed or complaining.

words.tr: n. 苛评；指责；限制；狭窄
words.ex: The doctor found a stricture in his esophagus.
words.ex_cn: 医生发现他的食管有狭窄。
words.en: A narrowing or constriction of a tube, duct, or passage in the body.

words.tr:
n. 寓言；神话传说；无稽之谈
v. 虚构
words.ex: The old man told a fable about a fox and a crow.
words.ex_cn: 老人讲了一个关于狐狸和乌鸦的寓言。
words.en: A fable is a short story that typically features animals as characters and conveys a moral lesson.

words.ex: He glowered at the boy who broke his vase.
words.ex_cn: 他怒视着打碎他花瓶的那个男孩。
words.en: If you glower at someone or something, you look at them in an angry way.

words.ex: He took an oath to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓要说出真相。
words.en: An oath is a formal promise, especially one made in a court of law or a religious ceremony, or a swear word.

words.ex: The crowd began to heckle the speaker during the debate.
words.ex_cn: 在辩论期间，观众开始嘲笑那位演讲者。
words.en: To heckle someone means to interrupt them while they are speaking, especially in a public situation, by shouting out questions or comments, often in order to challenge or embarrass them.

words.tr: v. 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提取；蒸馏出；提炼
words.ex: They distill water to remove impurities.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过蒸馏去除水中的杂质。
words.en: To distill a liquid means to purify it by heating it until it becomes a gas and then cooling it so that it becomes a liquid again. This process can also be used to extract the essential elements or meanings from something.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.tr: adj. 相接的；相邻的；接壤的
words.ex: The two countries are contiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家是相邻的。
words.en: Being in contact; touching or next to each other.

words.ex: He is thinking about metaphysical questions.
words.ex_cn: 他正在思考形而上学的问题。
words.en: Metaphysical means relating to metaphysics, which is the branch of philosophy that deals with the first principles of things, including abstract concepts such as being, knowing, substance, cause, identity, time, and space.

words.tr: adj. 变化多端的；千变万化的
words.ex: He is protean in his interests, changing often.
words.ex_cn: 他对兴趣变化多端，经常改变。
words.en: Able to change frequently or easily; versatile.

words.ex: She added sage to the stuffing for Thanksgiving dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她在感恩节晚餐的填料中加入了鼠尾草。
words.en: A sage is a person who is regarded as being very wise, especially someone who is known for their good judgment and deep understanding of life.

words.ex: The experience was a salutary lesson in the importance of preparation.
words.ex_cn: 这次经历是一个关于准备重要性的有益教训。
words.en: A salutary experience or warning is one that has a good effect or influence, especially by showing you the bad results of a particular action or behaviour.

words.ex: He has business acumen and makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他有商业洞察力，能做出明智的决定。
words.en: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain.

words.ex: The children played near the creek after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在小河旁玩耍。
words.en: A creek is a small, narrow stream or river.

words.ex: The sun vaporizes water from the lake.
words.ex_cn: 太阳把湖里的水蒸发了。
words.en: To convert or be converted into vapor.

words.tr: adj. 假情假义的；油腔滑调的
words.ex: His unctuous manner made me uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他油腔滑调的态度让我感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as unctuous, you are critical of them because they seem to be full of praise, kindness, or interest, but in a way that is not sincere.

words.tr: adj. 无赖的；低俗的；放荡不羁的
words.ex: The raffish man stole money from the old woman.
words.ex_cn: 那个无赖的男人从那位老太太那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as raffish, you mean that they are unconventional and attractive in a way that is slightly disreputable.

words.tr: adj. 贫血的；患贫血症的；衰弱无力的；无生气的
words.ex: He looks anemic after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病很久后看起来很苍白。
words.en: If someone is anemic, they are suffering from anemia, which means they have a lower than normal number of red blood cells or hemoglobin, making them feel tired and weak.

words.ex: His prolix speech made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他冗长的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: Using or containing too many words; tediously lengthy.

words.tr: v. 挑剔；吹毛求疵；鸡蛋里挑骨头
words.ex: She tends to nitpick about small details.
words.ex_cn: 她倾向于对小细节吹毛求疵。
words.en: To nitpick means to criticize or find fault with someone or something in a petty or fussy way.

words.ex: The soup was palatable after adding salt.
words.ex_cn: 加了盐后，汤变得可口美味了。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as palatable, you mean that it tastes pleasant.

words.tr: n. 饶舌之人；空话连篇的人
words.ex: He is a windbag who talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他是个爱说废话的人，话太多了。
words.en: A person who talks at length but says little of any value.

words.ex: We should conserve water in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们应在日常生活中节约用水。
words.en: To conserve something means to protect it from harm, loss, or change, especially in order to preserve it for the future.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.tr: adj. 无情的；冷酷的；残忍的；
words.ex: The ruthless boss fired employees without warning.
words.ex_cn: 这位无情的老板未经警告就解雇了员工。
words.en: If you say that someone is ruthless, you mean that you disapprove of them because they are very harsh or cruel, and will do anything that is necessary to achieve what they want.

words.tr: v. 同意；继承；即位；加入
words.ex: He acceded to their request.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了他们的请求。
words.en: If you accede to someone's request, you do what they ask.

words.tr:
v. 衰落；减弱；缺；亏
n. 衰退；减弱；缺；亏
words.ex: The moon begins to wane after the full moon.
words.ex_cn: 满月之后，月亮开始变暗。
words.en: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.ex: He bought equity in a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一家科技公司的股票。
words.en: Equity is the quality of being fair and impartial.

words.ex: The cat got entangled in the string.
words.ex_cn: 猫被绳子缠住了。
words.en: If something is entangled in something else, it is caught or twisted around it, or mixed with it so that it is difficult to separate the two things.

words.ex: He showed great temerity by challenging the expert without any preparation.
words.ex_cn: 他没有做任何准备就挑战专家，显得非常鲁莽。
words.en: If you say that someone has the temerity to do something, you are annoyed about something they have done which you think took a lot of nerve.

words.ex: She adores her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她非常喜爱她的弟弟。
words.en: If you adore someone, you feel great love and admiration for them.

words.ex: He is known for his probity in business.
words.ex_cn: 他以商业中的正直著称。
words.en: Probity is the quality of having strong moral principles and honesty.

words.ex: He crumpled the paper in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他把纸揉皱了。
words.en: If you crumple something such as paper or cloth, or if it crumples, it is squashed and becomes full of untidy creases and folds.

words.tr:
n. 锻造车间；
v. 建立（联系等）；
words.ex: The blacksmith works in the forge every morning.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠每天早上都在锻造车间工作。
words.en: To forge something means to create it, especially by using considerable effort or skill. It can also mean to make or produce something, especially with some difficulty or effort. Additionally, it refers to the act of making a copy or imitation of something with the intent to deceive.

words.tr: adj. 能吃苦耐劳的；耐寒的；
words.ex: He is a hardy farmer who works in the field all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个能吃苦耐劳的农民，整天在田里干活。
words.en: Someone who is hardy is strong and able to cope with difficult conditions.

words.tr:
v. 吹嘘；自夸
n. 吹嘘；自夸
words.ex: He likes to vaunt his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢炫耀他的新车。
words.en: To boast about or praise (something) excessively.

words.ex: The teacher gave students discretion to choose their own topic.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了学生自行选择题目的权利。
words.en: Discretion is the quality of behaving in a quiet and controlled way without drawing attention to yourself or giving away personal or private information.

words.tr: n. 弹幕射击；掩护炮火；拦河坝
words.ex: The soldiers faced a barrage of bullets.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们面对着一阵弹雨。
words.en: A barrage is a heavy and continuous bombardment of gunfire or a dam built across a river to control the flow of water.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍无度的；行为不检点的；放荡的
n. 放荡的人；恣意挥霍的人
words.ex: His profligate lifestyle led to his financial ruin.
words.ex_cn: 他放荡的生活方式导致了他经济上的破产。
words.en: Someone who is profligate spends too much money or uses too much of something.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；起破坏作用的
n. 腐蚀性物品
words.ex: The acid is corrosive and can damage metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种酸具有腐蚀性，会损坏金属。
words.en: A corrosive substance is able to destroy solid materials by a chemical reaction.

words.ex: The old engine spluttered and then stopped.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧引擎发出劈啪声，然后熄火了。
words.en: If someone splutters, they make short sounds and have difficulty speaking clearly, for example because they are embarrassed or angry.

words.ex: The cacophony of car horns made it hard to think.
words.ex_cn: 汽车喇叭的刺耳噪音让人难以思考。
words.en: A cacophony is a mixture of loud and usually unpleasant sounds.

words.ex: The child excoriated his knee when he fell on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子摔倒在粗糙的地面上，膝盖擦伤了。
words.en: To excoriate someone or something means to criticize them severely.

words.tr: v. 敷衍；拖延；见风驶舵
words.ex: He decided to temporize until he had more information.
words.ex_cn: 他决定拖延时间，直到获得更多信息。
words.en: To temporize means to delay making a decision or giving a definite answer in order to gain time or avoid committing oneself.

words.tr: adj. 苍白的；暗淡的；无生气的
words.ex: Her face was pallid after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 久病之后，她的脸色变得苍白。
words.en: If you describe something such as a performance or a piece of writing as pallid, you mean that it is weak and not at all exciting or interesting.

words.tr:
adj. 甜得发腻的；令人腻烦的
v. 感到腻烦；“cloy”的现在分词
words.ex: The cloying sweetness of the cake made me sick.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕过于甜腻的味道让我感到恶心。
words.en: If you describe something as cloying, you mean that it is so sweet or sentimental that it is unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；讨厌的；抵触的
words.ex: The smell was repugnant.
words.ex_cn: 那气味令人厌恶。
words.en: If you think that something is horrible and disgusting, you can say that it is repugnant.

words.tr: adj. 要求高的；费力的； v. 需要；“demand”的现在分词；
words.ex: The job is demanding because it needs long hours and high focus.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作要求高，因为它需要长时间工作和高度专注。
words.en: Requiring much effort or attention; exacting.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.ex: The gangly boy stumbled as he walked.
words.ex_cn: 这个瘦高个男孩走路时绊倒了。
words.en: If you describe someone as gangly, you mean that they are tall, thin, and rather awkward in their movements.

words.ex: He wants to expedite the process.
words.ex_cn: 他想加快这个过程。
words.en: To expedite something means to make it happen or be done more quickly.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 后勤人员；附加项目
words.ex: The ancillary staff help the doctors in the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 辅助人员在医院里帮助医生。
words.en: Ancillary means providing necessary support to the primary activities or operation of an organization, system, etc.

words.ex: The fringe of the forest is full of wildflowers.
words.ex_cn: 森林的边缘长满了野花。
words.en: The outer, marginal, or extreme part of an area, group, or sphere of activity.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；暗中行事的
words.ex: He made a clandestine meeting with his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他与朋友进行了一次秘密会面。
words.en: Kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.tr:
n. 针脚；缝线；一针
v. 缝；缝合
words.ex: She sews a stitch to fix the tear.
words.ex_cn: 她缝一针来补破洞。
words.en: A stitch is a piece of thread that has been used to sew the edges of a wound together. It can also refer to a loop of thread or yarn resulting from a single pass or movement of the needle in sewing, knitting, or crocheting.

words.ex: He is an avid reader of mystery novels.
words.ex_cn: 他热衷于阅读侦探小说。
words.en: If you say that someone is avid for something, you mean that they are very eager to get it.

words.tr: adj. 拒不服从的；藐视法庭的
words.ex: He was contumacious and refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他桀骜不驯，拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If someone is contumacious, they are stubbornly or willfully disobedient to authority.

words.tr: n. 小花饰；简介；（表演）片段
words.ex: She drew a small vignette on the corner of the letter.
words.ex_cn: 她在信的角落画了一个小花饰。
words.en: A vignette is a brief evocative description, account, or episode.

words.ex: The teacher used a pointer to show the map on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一根指物棒指着墙上的地图。
words.en: A pointer is a piece of advice or information which helps you to understand a situation or to find a way of making progress.

words.tr:
adj. 偏执狂的；患妄想狂的；过分猜疑的
n. 偏执狂患者；妄想症患者
words.ex: He is paranoid that someone is watching him.
words.ex_cn: 他总觉得有人在监视他。
words.en: If you say that someone is paranoid, you mean that they are extremely suspicious and afraid of other people.

words.ex: He will impugn the witness's honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他将质疑证人的诚实性。
words.en: To impugn means to challenge as false or questionable; to cast doubt upon.

words.ex: He spurned the offer because it was too low.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个提议，因为报酬太低。
words.en: If you spurn someone or something, you reject them with contempt.

words.tr:
adj. 蛮勇的；鲁莽大胆的
n. 鲁莽大胆的人
words.ex: He is a daredevil rider who jumps over cars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个蛮勇的骑手，会跳过汽车。
words.en: A daredevil is someone who enjoys doing dangerous things and taking risks.

words.ex: The loud noise roused him from sleep.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音把他从睡梦中唤醒了。
words.en: If someone rouses you when you are sleeping or if you rouse, you wake up. / To rouse someone means to make them stop doing something and start doing something else.

words.ex: The priest gave a short homily after the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 祷告后，牧师做了一个简短的讲道。
words.en: A homily is a religious discourse which is intended to edify a congregation, typically given by a priest or minister during a service.

words.tr:
adj. 健壮的；硬朗的
v. 强拉硬拖
words.ex: He is still hale at age 80.
words.ex_cn: 他80岁了依然身体健康。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially an old person, as hale, you mean that they are healthy.

words.tr: adj. 赞美的；赞赏的；称赞的
words.ex: The teacher gave a laudatory remark about his effort.
words.ex_cn: 老师对他的努力给予了赞扬的评价。
words.en: If something is laudatory, it expresses praise.

words.ex: The prosecution brought evidence against the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 起诉方提供了针对嫌疑人的证据。
words.en: The act or process of holding a trial against a person who is accused of a crime to see if they are guilty.

words.ex: The expansive desert stretches for miles.
words.ex_cn: 广阔的沙漠延伸数英里。
words.en: If you describe something such as a period of time or a piece of writing as expansive, you mean that it is very long or detailed.

words.ex: The barbarous act shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这野蛮的行为震惊了所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as barbarous, you mean that it is extremely cruel or uncivilized.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.ex: They had an amicable talk after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵之后，他们进行了一次友好的交谈。
words.en: When people have an amicable relationship, they are pleasant towards each other and solve their problems without arguing.

words.ex: The diver submerge to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员潜水去探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: To submerge something means to put it below the surface of a liquid, especially water. If something submerges, it goes below the surface of a liquid.

words.tr:
n. 审查员；检查员
v. 检查；审查
words.ex: The censor removed the bad words from the movie.
words.ex_cn: 审查员从电影中删除了粗俗用语。
words.en: A censor is a person who supervises conduct and morals: in particular, one who examines books, films, or other material for objectionable matter.

words.ex: Her smile heartened the tired students.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑鼓舞了疲惫的学生。
words.en: If someone is heartened by something, it encourages them and makes them cheerful.

words.tr:
adj. 有自动保险装置的；具有自动防止故障性能的
n. 故障自动保险；事故保险
words.ex: The system is designed to be fail-safe in case of emergency.
words.ex_cn: 该系统设计为在紧急情况下自动防故障。
words.en: A fail-safe device or system is one that has been designed so that if it stops working or something else goes wrong, it will not cause any harm or damage.

words.ex: The school has a hierarchical system.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个等级制度。
words.en: A hierarchical system or organization is one in which people have different ranks or positions, depending on how important they are.

words.tr: n. 头脑简单的人；傻瓜；笨蛋
words.ex: He is a simpleton who believes everything he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他是个傻瓜，什么都信。
words.en: A simpleton is someone who is not very intelligent and who is easily tricked or deceived.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；造成伤害的
words.ex: Smoking has deleterious effects on your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is deleterious has a harmful effect on something, especially on a person's health.

words.tr: adj. 不能减缩的；无法减轻的
words.ex: This fraction is irreducible.
words.ex_cn: 这个分数是最简形式。
words.en: If you describe something as irreducible, you mean that it cannot be made smaller or simpler.

words.ex: He practices his religion every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都实践自己的宗教信仰。
words.en: Religion is the belief in and worship of a superhuman controlling power, especially a personal God or gods.

words.ex: The trial was a farce.
words.ex_cn: 这场审判是一场闹剧。
words.en: A farce is a comedy that aims at entertaining the audience through situations that are highly exaggerated, extravagant, and thus improbable.

words.ex: The team showed great camaraderie during the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队在比赛中展现了深厚的友爱。
words.en: A feeling of good friendship among the people in a group.

words.tr: adj. 沉重的；笨重的；沉闷的
words.ex: He carried a ponderous box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他搬着一个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: Something that is ponderous is very heavy or is very slow and clumsy because of its weight or size.

words.tr: n. 前任；前辈；原有事物
words.ex: He became the new manager, replacing his predecessor.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了新经理，接替了他的前任。
words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.ex: He gave a vehement reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了激烈的回答。
words.en: If a person or their actions or comments are vehement, the person has very strong feelings or opinions and expresses them forcefully.

words.tr: n. 分水岭；集水区；转折点
words.ex: The river forms a watershed between two valleys.
words.ex_cn: 这条河构成了两个山谷之间的分水岭。
words.en: A watershed is an event or period that is important because it represents a big change in how people do or think about something.

words.ex: He shows narcissism by always talking about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他总是谈论自己，表现出自恋。
words.en: Narcissism is the habit of always thinking about yourself and your appearance and abilities, and believing that you are better than other people.

words.ex: Strong foundations undergird the old bridge.
words.ex_cn: 坚固的地基加强了这座旧桥。
words.en: To provide a strong foundation or support for something.

words.ex: He tried to seduce her with flowers and gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和礼物引诱她。
words.en: To seduce someone means to persuade them to do something, especially something wrong or unwise, by making it seem attractive or exciting.

words.ex: The thief tried to waylay the man on the dark street.
words.ex_cn: 小偷试图在黑暗的街道上拦住那个男人。
words.en: To lie in wait for and attack from ambush

words.ex: The magnitude of this decision will affect everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的重要性会影响每个人。
words.en: Magnitude refers to the great size or extent of something, or the importance of something.

words.tr:
n. 供过于求；过量
v. 使充满；过量供应
words.ex: The market has a glut of cheap phones.
words.ex_cn: 市场上廉价手机泛滥。
words.en: An excessive supply of something, more than is needed, wanted, or can be used; to supply or fill to excess.

words.ex: He was a faithful disciple of the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是老师的一名忠实弟子。
words.en: A disciple is a follower or student of a teacher, leader, or philosopher.

words.ex: He tries to attune his ears to the quiet sound.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让自己的耳朵适应那细微的声音。
words.en: If you attune your ear or your senses to something, you become used to it and can recognize it or understand it.

words.ex: He is apprehensive about the test.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试感到担忧。
words.en: Anxious or fearful that something bad or unpleasant will happen.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.tr: v. 废除；取消；宣告无效
words.ex: The court will annul the marriage.
words.ex_cn: 法院将宣布婚姻无效。
words.en: To annul something means to declare it invalid or to officially say that it no longer exists.

words.tr: adj. 自由自在的；无拘束的
words.ex: He is footloose after quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他辞掉工作后变得自由自在。
words.en: If you describe someone as footloose, you mean that they have no responsibilities or commitments, and are therefore free to do what they want and go where they want.

words.ex: She added a mint leaf to her drink.
words.ex_cn: 她在饮料里加了一片薄荷叶。
words.en: Mint is a plant with fresh-tasting leaves. It is also the place where coins are made, or the act of making coins.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.ex: He spoke with fervor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Fervor is intense and passionate feeling.

words.tr: adj. 厌恶人类的；不愿与人来往的
words.ex: He was misanthropic and preferred solitude to social gatherings.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶人类，宁愿独处也不愿参加社交聚会。
words.en: If you describe someone as misanthropic, you mean that they do not like other people and try to avoid them.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.tr: v. 简述；预示；勾画轮廓
words.ex: He adumbrated the plan in a few words.
words.ex_cn: 他用几句话简述了这个计划。
words.en: To give a faint indication or suggestion of something; to outline or sketch.

words.ex: He showed great enthusiasm for learning English.
words.ex_cn: 他对学习英语表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Enthusiasm is a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something and a desire to become involved in it.

words.ex: His perfidy shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的背信弃义让所有人震惊。
words.en: Perfidy is the act of deliberately betraying someone's trust; treachery.

words.ex: The priest gave a long sermon about kindness.
words.ex_cn: 牧师做了一场关于仁爱的长时间布道。
words.en: A sermon is a talk on a religious or moral subject, especially one given during a church service.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；可怜的；郁郁不乐的
words.ex: Her lugubrious expression made everyone feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 她那悲哀的表情让每个人都感到难过。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is lugubrious, you mean that they are sad and solemn.

words.tr: adj. 唐吉诃德式的；不切实际的
words.ex: He made a quixotic effort to fix the broken bridge with sticks and glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用树枝和胶水试图修复那座破桥，这真是异想天开。
words.en: If you describe someone's ideas or plans as quixotic, you mean that they are imaginative or hopeful but unrealistic.

words.ex: He tried to mollify his angry friend with an apology.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用道歉来安抚他生气的朋友。
words.en: To mollify someone means to make them feel calmer and less angry, upset, or worried.

words.ex: The pigment in leaves changes color in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 叶子中的色素在秋天会变色。
words.en: A pigment is a substance that gives something a particular color.

words.tr: n. 前景；最显著的位置；
words.ex: The trees in the foreground are very tall.
words.ex_cn: 前景中的树很高。
words.en: The part of a view that is nearest to the observer, especially in a picture or photograph; the most important or prominent position.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.ex: The denouement of the story was surprising.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的结局令人惊讶。
words.en: The final part of a play, movie, or narrative in which the strands of the plot are drawn together and matters are explained or resolved.

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: His coat is threadbare from many years of use.
words.ex_cn: 他的外套因为用了多年而变得破旧。
words.en: Worn out by overuse; shabby and old.

words.ex: The wicked witch cast a spell on the prince.
words.ex_cn: 邪恶的女巫对王子施了咒语。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as wicked, you mean that they are very bad, immoral, or cruel.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
words.en: Camouflage is the way in which some animals are colored and shaped so that they cannot easily be seen in their natural surroundings.

words.ex: He wants to study psychology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他想在大学学习心理学。
words.en: Psychology is the scientific study of the human mind and the reasons for people's behaviour.

words.ex: His lapse in judgment caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: A lapse is a temporary failure or a slight error, or the process by which something gradually passes into a different state, especially a worse one.

words.tr: n. 愤世嫉俗者；悲观者；怀疑者
words.ex: He is a cynic who never believes in good intentions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不相信任何善意的愤世嫉俗者。
words.en: A cynic is someone who believes that people are motivated purely by self-interest rather than acting for honorable or unselfish reasons.

words.ex: The profundity of his insights left the audience speechless.
words.ex_cn: 他见解的深刻让观众无言以对。
words.en: Profundity refers to the quality of being profound, which means having deep insight or understanding, or being very intense or extreme.

words.ex: His repertoire includes singing, dancing, and acting.
words.ex_cn: 他的全部才能包括唱歌、跳舞和表演。
words.en: A repertoire is all the plays, songs, pieces of music, etc. that a performer or group knows and can perform.

words.ex: He proved his innocence to vindicate his name.
words.ex_cn: 他证明了自己的清白以洗清自己的名声。
words.en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion.

words.tr: adj. 比喻的；象征的；写实的
words.ex: He used figurative language to describe his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他用了比喻性的语言来描述他的感受。
words.en: If you use a word or expression in a figurative sense, you use it with a more abstract or imaginative meaning than its ordinary literal one.

words.ex: The jury was sequestered during the trial.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团在审判期间被隔离。
words.en: To sequester means to isolate or hide away; it can also refer to the legal process of seizing property until a debt is paid or a dispute is resolved.

words.ex: She tried to requite his kindness with a thoughtful gift.
words.ex_cn: 她试图用一份贴心的礼物来回报他的好意。
words.en: To repay, return, or retaliate for something.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.tr: n. 特性；怪癖；奇异之物
words.ex: One peculiarity of the old house is its red door.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的一个特点是它的红门。
words.en: A peculiarity is a characteristic or quality that is distinctive or unique to a particular person, place, or thing.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；怠慢的；不留心的
words.ex: It would be remiss of me not to mention the importance of regular exercise.
words.ex_cn: 不提及定期锻炼的重要性，我会感到疏忽。
words.en: If someone is remiss, they are careless and do not do the things they are expected to do.

words.ex: The team worked in a harmonious way.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队以和谐的方式合作。
words.en: A harmonious situation, relationship, or agreement is one in which people are friendly and helpful to one another, and in which there is no serious disagreement or argument.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.tr: adj. 聪明的；时髦的；衣冠楚楚的；
words.ex: He is a smart student who solves math problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个聪明的学生，能快速解决数学问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as smart, you mean that they are clean, tidy, and stylish in their appearance.

words.ex: He felt ecstasy after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品后感到无比喜悦。
words.en: Ecstasy is a feeling of very great happiness.

words.ex: He follows a strict regimen to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循严格的作息计划来保持健康。
words.en: A regimen is a systematic plan or course of action intended to improve or maintain health, or a prescribed routine of diet, exercise, or manner of living.

words.tr:
n. 内容；含量；
adj. 满足的；
words.ex: The content of the video is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这个视频的内容非常有趣。
words.en: Content refers to the things that are held or included in something, or the state of being happy and satisfied.

words.tr: n. 堕落；道德败坏；腐化
words.ex: The depravity of his crimes shocked the community.
words.ex_cn: 他罪行的堕落程度震惊了整个社区。
words.en: Depravity is the state of being morally bad or evil.

words.tr: v. 不断请求；胡搅蛮缠
words.ex: He importunes his boss for a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他不断向老板请求加薪。
words.en: To importune someone means to ask them for something repeatedly and in a way that is annoying or troublesome.

words.tr: n. 意见分歧；纠纷；争执
words.ex: The team had dissension about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队对新计划有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement among people or groups, especially when it leads to conflict.

words.ex: He was considered a churl by his neighbors for his miserly ways.
words.ex_cn: 由于他的吝啬，邻居们都认为他是个吝啬鬼。
words.en: A churl is a rude, ill-bred person; a boor. It can also refer to a miserly person.

words.tr:
adv. 光明正大地
adj. 光明正大的
words.ex: He always plays aboveboard in business.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业中总是光明正大。
words.en: If something is aboveboard, it is done in an honest and open way without any attempt to deceive.

words.tr: adj. 不知情的；不经意的
words.ex: He was the unwitting victim of a prank.
words.ex_cn: 他是不知情的恶作剧受害者。
words.en: If someone is unwitting, they do not know or realize something.

words.ex: There was a large influx of tourists during the summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天期间涌入了大量游客。
words.en: An influx of people or things is a large number of them arriving somewhere at the same time.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.tr:
n. 浅薄的知识；一知半解；微量
v.  充内行；“smatter”的现在分词
words.ex: He has a smattering of knowledge in many subjects.
words.ex_cn: 他在许多科目上只有一知半解的知识。
words.en: A smattering of something is a small amount of it or a few things about it.

words.tr: v. 逐步渗透；逐渐灌输
words.ex: Parents try to instill good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To instill something in someone means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in their mind.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.tr: v. 专横；跋扈；盛气凌人
words.ex: He tries to domineer over his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图对弟弟发号施令。
words.en: To domineer means to rule over or control others in a harsh or arrogant way.

words.ex: The teacher reprehended the student for his disruptive behavior.
words.ex_cn: 老师因学生扰乱课堂的行为而责备他。
words.en: If you reprehend someone, you criticize them severely for their actions or behavior.

words.ex: The seeds germinate in warm soil.
words.ex_cn: 种子在温暖的土壤中发芽。
words.en: To germinate means to begin to grow or develop, especially for a seed or spore.

words.ex: They lionize the famous singer everywhere she goes.
words.ex_cn: 无论她去哪里，人们都把她当作名人追捧。
words.en: To treat someone as a celebrity or hero.

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.ex: The company made fraudulent claims about its product.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司对其产品做出了欺诈性的声明。
words.en: A fraudulent activity is deceitful or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 触觉的；能触知的；手感好的
words.ex: The child learns through tactile objects like blocks.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通过触觉物体如积木来学习。
words.en: Relating to the sense of touch; perceptible by touch.

words.tr: n. 喧闹作乐的人；狂欢者
words.ex: The roisterer laughed loudly at the party.
words.ex_cn: 那个喧闹的人在派对上大声笑。
words.en: A roisterer is someone who enjoys noisy, lively, and often rowdy behavior, typically in a social setting.

words.ex: His speech was full of bombast and little truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满空洞的豪言壮语，却缺乏真实内容。
words.en: Bombast is speech or writing that sounds grand or important but has little meaning.

words.tr: adj. 有浓烈气味的；扑鼻的；有刺激性的
words.ex: The lemonade has a tangy taste.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬水有酸味。
words.en: A tangy flavor is pleasantly strong and sharp.

words.ex: The walls are beige.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁是米黄色的。
words.en: A pale sandy yellowish-brown color.

words.ex: He will hearken to his teacher's advice.
words.ex_cn: 他会听从老师的建议。
words.en: To listen attentively or give heed to something or someone.

words.ex: The stars seem eternal in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中的星星看起来是永久的。
words.en: If something is eternal, it lasts forever.

words.tr:
v. 空谈；废话；阿谀奉承
n. 谈判；空谈；奉承
words.ex: The negotiators engaged in a lengthy palaver to reach a compromise.
words.ex_cn: 谈判代表们进行了长时间的谈判以达成妥协。
words.en: Palaver is prolonged and idle discussion, often intended to avoid addressing a problem directly.

words.tr:
v. 搜寻；（动物）觅食；
n. 饲料；草料；
words.ex: The bear forages for berries in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这只熊在森林里搜寻浆果。
words.en: If you forage, you search for food or other supplies. Forage can also refer to food for animals, especially when it is grown or collected.

words.tr:
adj. 忠实的；坚定的
v. 止住（血等的）流出
words.ex: He is a staunch supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的坚定支持者。
words.en: A staunch person is someone who is very loyal and firm in their beliefs or support for someone or something.

words.tr: n. 派系；派系斗争；内讧
words.ex: The faction argued loudly about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别就新规定激烈争论。
words.en: A faction is a group of people within a larger group who have different opinions and beliefs from the rest of the group.

words.tr:
n. 折痕；皱痕
v. 起皱；弄皱
words.ex: The paper has a deep crease from folding.
words.ex_cn: 这张纸因为折叠而有一道深深的折痕。
words.en: A crease is a line or mark made on cloth or paper when it is folded or crushed.

words.ex: A small rivulet flows through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 一条小溪流过森林。
words.en: A very small stream.

words.tr:
v. 缓期执行；暂缓处刑
n. 缓刑；暂缓
words.ex: The judge gave him a reprieve until next month.
words.ex_cn: 法官给了他一个延期，直到下个月。
words.en: If someone who has been sentenced in a court is given a reprieve, their punishment is officially delayed or cancelled.

words.tr:
v. 非法侵入；侵扰；冒犯
n. 非法进入；冒犯
words.ex: He trespasses on private land.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自进入私人土地。
words.en: To trespass is to enter someone's land or property without their permission.

words.ex: The book is 10 inches long.
words.ex_cn: 这本书长10英寸。
words.en: An inch is a unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot.

words.ex: The village holds a rite every spring.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一场仪式。
words.en: A rite is a traditional ceremony that is carried out by a particular group or society, especially a religious one.

words.tr:
v. 叛乱；反叛；（使）厌恶
n. 叛乱；厌恶；反感
words.ex: The people revolt against the unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 人们反抗不公平的规则。
words.en: If a large number of people revolt, they refuse to be controlled or ruled, and take action against authority, often violent action.

words.tr: adj. 清洁的；无瑕疵的；无过失的
words.ex: The kitchen was immaculate after she cleaned it.
words.ex_cn: 她打扫后，厨房非常干净。
words.en: If you describe something as immaculate, you mean that it is extremely clean, tidy, or neat.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.ex: The argument started small but soon escalate.
words.ex_cn: 争论起初很小，但很快逐步升高。
words.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity.

words.tr: adj. 非物质的；无形的；不重要的
words.ex: The color is immaterial to the function.
words.ex_cn: 颜色对功能无关紧要。
words.en: If you say that something is immaterial, you mean that it is not important or not relevant.

words.ex: He works in a small studio near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园附近的一个小工作室工作。
words.en: A studio is a room where an artist, photographer, or designer works, or a place where movies or television programs are made.

words.tr: v. 弥漫于；充满；扩散；布满
words.ex: The sunset suffuses the sky with orange light.
words.ex_cn: 日落将天空染成橙色。
words.en: If something such as a colour, emotion, or light suffuses a person or thing, it gradually spreads over or through them.

words.ex: This lock is foolproof and easy to use.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁是万无一失的，而且容易使用。
words.en: A foolproof plan, system, or method is so well designed that it cannot go wrong or be used wrongly.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.ex: He used a euphemism to say he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个委婉语来表示他失业了。
words.en: A euphemism is a polite word or expression that is used to refer to things which people may find upsetting or embarrassing to talk about.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.tr: adj. 极神圣的；神圣不可侵犯的
words.ex: The church's rules were considered sacrosanct and unchangeable.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的规定被认为是神圣不可侵犯的，不可改变的。
words.en: If you describe something as sacrosanct, you mean that it is considered to be special and should not be changed or interfered with.

words.ex: He posits that the earth is round.
words.ex_cn: 他提出地球是圆的。
words.en: To posit something is to suggest it as a basic fact or principle from which a further idea is formed or developed.

words.ex: My passport will expire next month.
words.ex_cn: 我的护照下个月到期。
words.en: If something such as a contract or a visa expires, it comes to an end or is no longer valid.

words.ex: He uses hyperbole when he says he is dying of hunger.
words.ex_cn: 当他说到自己快饿死了时，他用了夸张的说法。
words.en: Hyperbole is a way of speaking or writing that makes someone or something sound bigger, better, more, etc. than they are.

words.tr: v. 使冲昏头脑；弄糊涂；使着迷
words.ex: He is infatuated with his new classmate.
words.ex_cn: 他迷上了他的新同学。
words.en: To inspire with a foolish or extravagant love or admiration.

words.ex: The committee issued a remonstrance against the proposed changes.
words.ex_cn: 委员会对拟议的变更提出了抗议。
words.en: A remonstrance is a formal statement of protest or complaint.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.tr:
adj. 缩成皱纹的；使起波状的
v. （使）起皱褶；“corrugate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The box is made of corrugated cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是由波纹纸板制成的。
words.en: Something that is corrugated has parallel rows of folds that look like a series of waves when viewed from the edge.

words.ex: The police tried to subdue the angry man.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图制服那个愤怒的人。
words.en: To subdue someone or something means to bring them under control by using force or persuasion.

words.ex: The serpentine road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯弯曲曲的路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: Something that is serpentine is curving and winding in shape, like a snake when it moves.

words.ex: The roof is made of slate.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶是由板岩制成的。
words.en: A slate is a fine-grained, foliated, homogeneous metamorphic rock derived from an original shale-type sedimentary rock composed of clay or volcanic ash through low-grade regional metamorphism. It is the finest grained foliated metamorphic rock. Foliation may not correspond to the original sedimentary layering, but instead is in planes perpendicular to the direction of metamorphic compression.

words.ex: The pirate sailed the sea with a black flag.
words.ex_cn: 海盗带着黑旗在海上航行。
words.en: A pirate is someone who attacks and robs ships at sea. The term can also refer to someone who illegally copies and distributes software, music, or films.

words.ex: He believes in an egalitarian society where everyone is equal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信一个人人平等的平等主义社会。
words.en: Egalitarian is used to describe something that is based on the principle that all people are equal and deserve equal rights and opportunities.

words.tr: adj. 直截了当的；直率的；坦白的
words.ex: He is forthright about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他坦率地承认自己的错误。
words.en: If you describe someone as forthright, you admire them because they show clearly and strongly what they think and feel.

words.tr: adj. 漫不经心的；无忧无虑的
words.ex: He gave a blithe smile and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他漫不经心地笑了笑，然后走开了。
words.en: If you describe someone as blithe, you mean that they are carefree and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.tr: n. 滑稽地模仿；哄骗；戏弄；讽刺；
words.ex: The movie is a spoof of classic horror films.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对经典恐怖片的滑稽模仿。
words.en: A spoof is a humorous imitation of something, typically a film or a particular genre of film, in which its characteristic features are exaggerated for comic effect.

words.ex: He doffed his hat as a sign of respect.
words.ex_cn: 他脱帽以示敬意。
words.en: To remove an item of clothing, especially a hat.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.tr: adj. 衰弱的；衰败的；软弱的
words.ex: The old king was effete and could not lead.
words.ex_cn: 这位老国王虚弱无能，无法领导。
words.en: No longer productive or effective; lacking the power or will to achieve or succeed.

words.ex: The apple plummeted from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上垂直落下。
words.en: If an amount, rate, or price plummets, it decreases quickly by a large amount.

words.ex: He composes music in his spare time.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间创作音乐。
words.en: To compose something means to make it by combining parts or elements.

words.ex: He tried to dissuade her from quitting her job.
words.ex_cn: 他试图劝她不要辞掉工作。
words.en: If you dissuade someone from doing something, you persuade them not to do it.

words.ex: The sun will desiccate the leaves in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天阳光会把叶子晒干。
words.en: To remove the moisture from something, typically in order to preserve it.

words.tr:
n. 撑杆；支柱
v. 趾高气扬地走；昂首阔步
words.ex: The bridge has metal struts to support the weight.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有金属撑杆来支撑重量。
words.en: If someone struts, they walk in a proud way, with their chest out and trying to look important.

words.ex: The village sent a tribute of grain to the king.
words.ex_cn: 村庄向国王进贡了谷物。
words.en: A tribute is something that you say, do, or make to show your admiration and respect for someone.

words.tr: adj. 诡诈的；诡秘的；心照不宣的
words.ex: The sly fox stole the chicken at night.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸在夜里偷了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is sly is clever and good at deceiving people in a way that is not easily noticed.

words.ex: He used a simile to compare her eyes to stars.
words.ex_cn: 他用了明喻把她的眼睛比作星星。
words.en: A simile is a figure of speech that directly compares two different things, usually by employing the words 'like' or 'as'.

words.tr:
adj. 平民的；粗俗的
n. 平民；下层人；老百姓
words.ex: The speech was criticized for its plebeian language.
words.ex_cn: 这篇演讲因其粗俗的语言而受到批评。
words.en: A plebeian is a member of the general populace, especially one of the common people of ancient Rome. As an adjective, it describes something that is common, ordinary, or vulgar.

words.tr: adj. 有附带条件的；有附文的；临时的
words.ex: The agreement was provisory and subject to change.
words.ex_cn: 该协议是附带条件的，可能会发生变化。
words.en: A provisory measure or arrangement is one that is made or done for the time being, especially until something more permanent can be arranged.

words.tr: n. 再发；重陷；故态复萌；
words.ex: He had a relapse after stopping his medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他停药后病情复发了。
words.en: If someone relapses, they return to a less advanced state, or to a previous way of behaving that they wanted to change.

words.ex: The cellular structure of plants is very small.
words.ex_cn: 植物的细胞结构非常微小。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of cells; having a porous structure.

words.ex: He has scads of toy cars.
words.ex_cn: 他有大量的玩具车。
words.en: If you refer to scads of things or people, you are emphasizing that there are a lot of them.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.ex: His overbearing boss always tells him what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他专横的老板总是告诉他该做什么。
words.en: If you describe someone as overbearing, you mean that they behave in a very unpleasant way because they are too confident of their own importance.

words.tr: v. 暂停；中止；延期； suspending
words.ex: The school will suspend the class due to snow.
words.ex_cn: 由于下雪，学校将暂停课程。
words.en: If you suspend something, you delay it or stop it from happening for a while or until a decision is made about it.

words.tr: adj. 分离（性）的；（指连词）转折的
words.ex: The two ideas are disjunctive and cannot be combined.
words.ex_cn: 这两个想法是分离的，无法结合。
words.en: A disjunctive word or phrase is one that indicates a separation or contrast between the parts of a sentence.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.tr:
v. 眯着眼看；斜视
n. 斜视；一瞥
words.ex: He squints to see the small letters.
words.ex_cn: 他眯着眼睛看那些小字。
words.en: To squint means to look at something with your eyes partly closed in order to see better, or because of bright light. It can also refer to a condition where the eyes do not look in the same direction.

words.ex: The children caused a big commotion in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里制造了很大的喧闹。
words.en: A commotion is a lot of noise, confusion, and excitement.

words.ex: The punishment was condign for the crime committed.
words.ex_cn: 这个惩罚对于所犯的罪行来说是应得的。
words.en: Deserved; appropriate; fitting.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.ex: He wrote copious notes during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座期间写了大量的笔记。
words.en: Something that is copious exists in large amounts.

words.tr: v. 即兴创作；即兴表演；临时准备；
words.ex: He improvise a song on the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他即兴创作了一首钢琴曲。
words.en: If you improvise, you make or do something using whatever you have or without having planned it in advance.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.ex: He felt a palpitation after running fast.
words.ex_cn: 他快速跑步后感到心跳加速。
words.en: A palpitation is an unusually rapid, strong, or irregular heartbeat that you are aware of, often described as a fluttering or pounding sensation in the chest.

words.ex: The snake released venom into its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇向猎物释放了毒液。
words.en: Venom is a poisonous substance secreted by animals such as snakes and spiders, used for defense or to kill prey.

words.ex: His constant self-abasement made him seem weak and unconfident.
words.ex_cn: 他不断的自卑让他显得软弱和不自信。
words.en: Self-abasement is the act of belittling or degrading oneself, often excessively or unnecessarily.

words.ex: The police told everyone to evacuate the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察让所有人撤离大楼。
words.en: To evacuate means to remove people from a place of danger to a safer place.

words.tr: n. 良心的责备；后悔；悔恨
words.ex: He felt no compunction about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他撒谎骗朋友时毫无愧疚。
words.en: A feeling of guilt or moral scruple that prevents or follows the doing of something bad.

words.ex: The teacher gave timely help when I was stuck.
words.ex_cn: 当我遇到困难时，老师及时提供了帮助。
words.en: done or occurring at a favorable or useful time; opportune.

words.ex: He ignored the frivolous complaint and focused on the real issue.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个无关紧要的投诉，专注于真正的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as frivolous, you mean they behave in a silly or light-hearted way, rather than being serious and sensible.

words.ex: The plangent sound of the church bells echoed through the valley.
words.ex_cn: 教堂钟声的轰鸣声在山谷中回荡。
words.en: A plangent sound is loud, deep, and often sad.

words.ex: He plays the trumpet in the school band.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校乐队里吹喇叭。
words.en: A trumpet is a brass musical instrument with a flared bell and three valves, producing a bright, penetrating tone.

words.tr:
n. 同辈；同等的人；
v. 凝视；
words.ex: He feels comfortable talking to his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得和同辈交谈很自在。
words.en: A peer is someone who is equal to another in abilities, qualifications, age, background, or social status. As a verb, to peer means to look keenly or with difficulty at someone or something.

words.tr: n. 喧嚣；大混乱；大吵大闹
words.ex: The crowd created pandemonium when the winner was announced.
words.ex_cn: 当获胜者被宣布时，人群陷入了混乱。
words.en: Pandemonium is a situation in which there is a lot of noise and confusion because people are excited, angry, or frightened.

words.ex: Lying has serious consequences.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎会有严重的后果。
words.en: A consequence is a result or effect of an action or condition.

words.tr: adj. 敏感的；感情脆弱的；体贴的；善解人意的；
words.ex: He is sensitive to loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对大声响很敏感。
words.en: If you are sensitive to other people's needs, problems, or feelings, you understand and are aware of them.

words.tr: n. 少量；一点点；一小份
words.ex: He had a modicum of common sense.
words.ex_cn: 他有一点点常识。
words.en: A modicum of something, especially something that is good or desirable, is a small but useful or significant amount of it.

words.ex: He took a circuitous route to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他绕了远路以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A circuitous route, journey, or piece of writing is longer than it needs to be because it is not direct.

words.tr:
adj. 要求严格的；要求小心仔细的；苛求的
v. 强求；急需；要求；“exact”的现在分词
words.ex: He is an exacting teacher who wants perfect work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个要求严格的老师，要求完美无缺的作业。
words.en: requiring a lot of effort, care, or attention

words.ex: The apples ripen in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 苹果在秋天成熟。
words.en: When crops ripen or when the sun ripens them, they become ripe and ready to eat.

words.ex: The dark clouds looked ominous before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨来临前，乌云显得不祥。
words.en: If you describe something as ominous, you mean that it worries you because it makes you think that something unpleasant is going to happen.

words.tr: adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑剔的
words.ex: He made a captious comment about the small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对一个小错误发表了挑剔的评论。
words.en: Tending to find fault or raise petty objections.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.ex: The mobile table can be moved easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个可移动的桌子很容易搬动。
words.en: A mobile is something that can move or be moved easily.

words.ex: We will meet at the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将在公园见面。
words.en: To come into the presence of someone by chance or arrangement.

words.ex: She concatenates two strings to make one word.
words.ex_cn: 她把两个字符串连接成一个单词。
words.en: To link things together in a chain or series.

words.tr:
v. 神气十足地走；大摇大摆地走
n. 大摇大摆；神气十足
words.ex: He walks with swagger down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他大摇大摆地走在街上。
words.en: If someone swaggers, they walk in a very proud and confident way, often in a way that annoys other people.

words.tr:
v. 偷懒；称病；欺诈
n. 假金砖；懒汉；赝品
words.ex: He is goldbricking instead of working.
words.ex_cn: 他正在偷懒而不工作。
words.en: To avoid work or responsibility, especially by pretending to be busy or by shirking duties.

words.tr:
n. 合金
v. 把…铸成合金
words.ex: He made a strong alloy from copper and zinc.
words.ex_cn: 他用铜和锌制造了一种坚固的合金。
words.en: An alloy is a metal made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

words.tr: adj. 精明的；敏锐的；机灵的；
words.ex: He made a shrewd decision to buy the house low.
words.ex_cn: 他精明地决定低价买下这栋房子。
words.en: A shrewd person is able to understand and judge a situation quickly and to use this understanding to their own advantage.

words.ex: He decided to embark on a new career.
words.ex_cn: 他决定从事一份新职业。
words.en: To embark on something means to start it, especially something new, difficult, or exciting.

words.tr: adj. 北欧古字的；卢恩文的；神秘的
words.ex: He found an old stone with runic letters.
words.ex_cn: 他发现了一块刻有如尼文字的古老石头。
words.en: Runic refers to the ancient alphabets used by Germanic peoples before the adoption of the Latin alphabet, or something resembling these alphabets.

words.ex: The gland secrete sweat to cool the body.
words.ex_cn: 腺体分泌汗液来降温。
words.en: If part of a plant, animal, or human secretes a liquid or substance, it produces it.

words.tr: adj. 小气的；吝啬的；太节省的
words.ex: His parsimonious nature made him unpopular among colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他吝啬的本性使得他在同事中不受欢迎。
words.en: Someone who is parsimonious is very unwilling to spend money.

words.ex: The law will emancipate slaves.
words.ex_cn: 法律将解放奴隶。
words.en: To emancipate someone means to set them free from something that restricts their freedom to do what they want.

words.ex: He had to relinquish his seat to an old man.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不把座位让给一位老人。
words.en: If you relinquish something, such as power or control, you give it up, often unwillingly.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不连贯的；断续的
words.ex: He gave a desultory answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个漫无目的的回答。
words.en: Something that is desultory is done in an unplanned and disorganized way, and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: The corn has a dry husk around it.
words.ex_cn: 玉米外面有一层干外壳。
words.en: The outer covering of some fruits and seeds, especially when it is dry and hard.

words.tr: v. 充分满足，使饱享； 使厌腻
words.ex: The rich food sated her hunger.
words.ex_cn: 丰盛的食物满足了她的饥饿感。
words.en: To satisfy a desire or an appetite to the full.

words.ex: He tried to repress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you repress a feeling, you deliberately do not express it, often because it is considered unacceptable or inappropriate.

words.ex: The children laughed with mirth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们带着欢乐大笑。
words.en: Mirth is amusement which you express by laughing.

words.ex: The company must retrench to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司必须裁员以节省资金。
words.en: If a person or organization retrenches, they spend less money.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.tr:
n. 褶边；褶饰
v. 弄皱；弄乱；扰乱
words.ex: The dress has a pink ruffle at the bottom.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子的底部有一条粉色的褶边。
words.en: To ruffle something means to disturb its smoothness or neatness, making it uneven or messy.

words.tr: adj. 贪婪的；贪得无厌的；劫掠的
words.ex: The rapacious wolf ate all the food.
words.ex_cn: 贪婪的狼吃掉了所有食物。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as rapacious, you disapprove of their greedy or selfish behaviour.

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.ex: The violent news appalls her.
words.ex_cn: 这起暴力新闻令她震惊。
words.en: to fill with horror or dismay; shock deeply

words.ex: They have good rapport with their students.
words.ex_cn: 他们与学生关系友好。
words.en: A friendly relationship in which people understand each other very well.

words.tr:
adj. 疏远的；冷淡的
adv. 远离地
words.ex: He stayed aloof during the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上保持冷淡。
words.en: Someone who is aloof is not very friendly and does not like to spend time with other people.

words.tr:
adj. 代理的；代用的
n. 代理人；代用品
words.ex: He acted as a surrogate father to the child.
words.ex_cn: 他作为孩子的代理父亲。
words.en: A surrogate is a person or thing that takes the place of or acts for another, especially in a role or function that is typically filled by someone else.

words.ex: He was accused of purloining company funds.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控偷窃公司资金。
words.en: To purloin means to steal something, especially in a sneaky or stealthy manner.

words.ex: The track is elliptical in shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个跑道是椭圆形的。
words.en: Something that is elliptical has the shape of an ellipse or is characterized by the omission of words that are understood to be obvious.

words.ex: The police will interrogate the suspect tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 警察明天会审问嫌疑人。
words.en: To interrogate someone means to ask them a lot of questions for a long time in order to get information, sometimes using threats.

words.ex: He walks with a crutch after his accident.
words.ex_cn: 他事故后拄着拐杖走路。
words.en: A crutch is a stick with a handle and a part that fits under the arm, which you use to support your body if you are having difficulty in walking because of a foot or leg injury.

words.tr: n. 要求严格纪律的人；严格执行纪律者
words.ex: The sergeant was a martinet who insisted on absolute obedience from his troops.
words.ex_cn: 这位中士是一个严格执行纪律的人，他坚持要求他的部队绝对服从。
words.en: A martinet is someone who demands strict adherence to rules and discipline.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.tr: v. 给予选举权；释放（奴隶）
words.ex: The law will enfranchise all adults over 18.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律将赋予所有18岁以上成年人选举权。
words.en: To enfranchise someone means to give them the right to vote in elections.

words.tr: n. 收容所；避难所；精神病院；（政治）庇护
words.ex: The old building now serves as an asylum for the homeless.
words.ex_cn: 这栋旧建筑现在是无家可归者的收容所。
words.en: An asylum is a place where people who are in danger or who have no homes can go for safety and protection.

words.ex: He received kudos for winning the science competition.
words.ex_cn: 他因赢得科学竞赛而获得荣誉。
words.en: Praise and honor received for an achievement.

words.ex: The confluence of the two rivers created a fertile valley.
words.ex_cn: 两条河流的汇流形成了一个肥沃的山谷。
words.en: The confluence of two or more things is the junction or merging of them, often forming something greater or more complex.

words.ex: The fence safeguards the garden from animals.
words.ex_cn: 围栏保护花园免受动物侵扰。
words.en: A safeguard is a measure taken to protect someone or something from potential harm or danger.

words.tr:
n. 鱼饵；诱惑物
v. 下诱饵
words.ex: He used bread as bait to catch fish.
words.ex_cn: 他用面包当诱饵来钓鱼。
words.en: Bait is something which is used to attract fish or animals so that they can be caught. It can also refer to something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.ex: The pilot landed the plane safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员安全地降落了飞机。
words.en: A pilot is a person who operates the flying controls of an aircraft. Also, to pilot something means to test or introduce a new idea, product, etc., to see if it will be successful.

words.tr:
n. 树液；
v. 使逐渐耗竭；使削弱；
words.ex: The tree releases sap in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在春天流出树液。
words.en: Sap is the watery fluid that circulates in the vascular system of a plant, carrying nutrients and sugars. It can also refer to the vitality or energy of a person or thing.

words.tr: v. 摇摇欲坠；摇摆；玩跷跷板
words.ex: The child teeters on the edge of the pool.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在泳池边摇摇晃晃。
words.en: To move or balance unsteadily; sway back and forth.

words.ex: He shirks his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天逃避作业。
words.en: If someone shirks their duties or responsibilities, they deliberately avoid doing them.

words.tr:
adj. 多汞的；含汞的；易变的；灵活的；反复无常的
n. 汞制剂；水银剂
words.ex: His mercurial mood changes from happy to angry quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他多汞的情绪很快从高兴变到生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as mercurial, you mean that they frequently change their mind or mood without warning.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的
words.ex: Her performance was unexceptionable.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现无可挑剔。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unexceptionable, you mean that they are unlikely to be criticized or objected to, because they are very good, standard, or normal.

words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.tr: n. 物物交换；实物交易；
words.ex: They used barter to trade apples for eggs.
words.ex_cn: 他们用物物交换的方式用苹果换鸡蛋。
words.en: To trade goods or services without using money.

words.tr: v. 删去（书籍中不合适之处）
words.ex: The teacher expurgated the old book to remove bad words.
words.ex_cn: 老师删改了这本旧书，去掉了不好的词语。
words.en: To remove material that is considered improper or offensive from (a book, movie, etc.).

words.tr: v. 侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐丧失；削弱
words.ex: The wind erodes the sand slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢侵蚀着沙子。
words.en: If rock or soil erodes or is eroded by the weather, sea, or wind, it cracks and breaks so that it is gradually destroyed.

words.ex: He was punished for transgressing the law.
words.ex_cn: 他因违法而受到惩罚。
words.en: To transgress means to go beyond the limits of what is morally, socially, or legally acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.tr:
n. 信用；赊账；赞扬；贷款；荣誉；
v. 相信；
words.ex: He has good credit with the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他在银行有良好的信用。
words.en: If you are allowed credit, you are allowed to pay for goods or services several weeks or months after you have received them.

words.ex: The frosty grass sparkled in the morning sun.
words.ex_cn: 霜冻的草地在晨光中闪闪发亮。
words.en: If the weather is frosty, the temperature is below the freezing point of water and the ground is covered with frost.

words.ex: The joy was transitory, and soon he felt sad again.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是暂时的，不久他又感到悲伤了。
words.en: Something that is transitory lasts only for a short time.

words.tr:
adj. 无可名状的；难以区别的；无特征的；极普通的
n. 无以名状；不属任何类型的人
words.ex: The building was nondescript, with no special features.
words.ex_cn: 这栋建筑无可名状，没有任何特别的特征。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as nondescript, you mean that their appearance is rather dull, and not at all interesting or attractive.

words.ex: The teacher reproved the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责骂了他。
words.en: If you reprove someone, you speak angrily or seriously to them because they have behaved in a wrong or foolish way.

words.tr: adj. 糟糕透顶的；恶劣的；卑鄙的
words.ex: He said a vile thing to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友说了句卑鄙的话。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is vile, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant.

words.ex: He affixed a stamp to the envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他把邮票贴在信封上。
words.en: To attach, fasten, or join something to something else.

words.tr: n. 田园风景；田园生活；田园诗
words.ex: The small village was the perfect setting for an idyll.
words.ex_cn: 这个小村庄是田园诗的完美背景。
words.en: An idyll is a short poem or piece of prose that describes a peaceful or romantic scene, especially of rural life.

words.tr: adj. 病理学的；病理的；病态的
words.ex: The doctor found a pathological change in the tissue.
words.ex_cn: 医生在组织中发现了一种病理性的变化。
words.en: Pathological means relating to pathology, which is the study of diseases, or it can describe a behavior or condition that is extreme and not normal, often in a way that is harmful or undesirable.

words.tr: n. 帆布篷；雨篷；遮阳篷
words.ex: The awnings provided shade from the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 遮阳篷为人们提供了躲避烈日的阴凉处。
words.en: An awning is a piece of material attached to a building or a frame, which provides shelter from the sun or rain.

words.tr:
n. 栅栏；围栏
v. 用栅栏围住；用栅栏防卫
words.ex: The prisoners were locked in a wooden stockade.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯们被关在木制栅栏里。
words.en: A stockade is a defensive barrier made from upright wooden posts or stakes, especially as a temporary defense against attack.

words.tr: adj. 仆人的；枯燥的；琐碎的
words.ex: He did menial work to earn money.
words.ex_cn: 他做琐碎的工作来赚钱。
words.en: A menial task is one that is considered to be lowly or degrading, often involving physical work and requiring little skill or education.

words.tr: adj. 沉闷乏味的；忧郁的；凄凉的
words.ex: The weather was dreary and rainy all day.
words.ex_cn: 天气一整天都阴沉沉的，还下着雨。
words.en: If you describe something as dreary, you mean that it is dull, lifeless, or depressing.

words.ex: The teacher showed favoritism toward his favorite student.
words.ex_cn: 老师对他的最爱学生表现出偏袒。
words.en: The practice of giving unfair preferential treatment to one person or group at the expense of another.

words.ex: His rude behavior alienated his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的行为使朋友们疏远了他。
words.en: To cause someone to feel isolated or estranged; to transfer the ownership of property to another.

words.tr: v. 节省；过度缩减；吝啬
words.ex: She had to scrimp and save to afford the trip.
words.ex_cn: 她不得不精打细算，省吃俭用才能负担得起这次旅行。
words.en: To scrimp means to be very careful with money and to try to spend as little as possible.

words.ex: The nascent industry is growing quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个新生的产业正在迅速发展。
words.en: Nascent things or processes are just beginning, and are expected to become stronger or to grow bigger.

words.tr:
v. 睡眠
n. 睡眠（常复数）
words.ex: The baby fell into a deep slumber after feeding.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝喂完奶后进入了深深的睡眠。
words.en: Slumber is a state of sleep, especially one that is peaceful and restful.

words.ex: The theatrical lighting made the stage look magical.
words.ex_cn: 剧场的灯光让舞台显得神奇。
words.en: Theatrical means relating to the theatre or to the performance of plays. It can also describe behaviour that is exaggerated and intended to attract attention.

words.tr: adj. 流泪的；爱哭的；引人落泪的
words.ex: The lachrymose melody of the violin added to the somber atmosphere.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴哀伤的旋律增添了忧郁的气氛。
words.en: If you describe someone as lachrymose, you mean that they are sad or likely to cry easily.

words.tr:
n. 黄疸病；偏见
v. 使产生黄疸；使怀偏见
words.ex: The baby had jaundice and needed light therapy.
words.ex_cn: 这个婴儿患有黄疸，需要光疗。
words.en: Jaundice is a medical condition in which the skin and the whites of the eyes become yellow, caused by an excess of bile pigment in the blood.

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.ex: The scandal caused a dent in his reputation.
words.ex_cn: 这场丑闻削弱了他的声誉。
words.en: A dent is a hollow or depression in a surface, often caused by a blow or pressure.

words.ex: The nefarious thief stole money from the poor.
words.ex_cn: 那个极坏的贼从穷人那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe an activity as nefarious, you mean that it is wicked and immoral.

words.tr: n. 实践者；从业者；执业者；
words.ex: He is a medical practitioner who helps patients every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天帮助病人的医疗实践者。
words.en: A practitioner is someone who works in a particular profession, especially one that requires special training and skills.

words.tr:
adj. 逐字的；一字不差的
adv. 逐字地；一字不差地
words.ex: He repeated the words verbatim.
words.ex_cn: 他一字不差地重复了那些话。
words.en: Using exactly the same words as were used originally.

words.tr: n. 美食家；讲究饮食的人
words.ex: He is an epicure who loves fine food.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱美食的享乐者。
words.en: An epicure is a person who enjoys high-quality food and drink and is very knowledgeable about it.

words.ex: The guard is vigilant at night.
words.ex_cn: 这名守卫在夜里非常警惕。
words.en: Someone who is vigilant gives careful attention to a particular problem or situation and concentrates on noticing any danger or trouble that there might be.

words.ex: The axe will cleave the wood in two.
words.ex_cn: 斧头会把木头劈成两半。
words.en: To split or sever something, especially along a natural line or grain; to adhere firmly and closely or loyally and unwaveringly to something.

words.ex: His ostensible reason for leaving was sickness.
words.ex_cn: 他离开的表面原因是生病。
words.en: An ostensible reason or purpose seems to be the real one, but it is not.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；肿大；使扩张；使膨胀；
words.ex: The balloon distend when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充满空气时会膨胀。
words.en: If a part of your body distends or if you distend it, it becomes larger or swollen, often because of pressure from inside.

words.ex: She painted with great verve.
words.ex_cn: 她作画时充满热情。
words.en: If you say that someone has verve, you mean that they seem to have a lot of energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: The old factory is now a derelict building.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧工厂现在是一座破败的建筑。
words.en: If a building or a piece of land is derelict, it is not cared for and is in bad condition. A derelict person or thing is one that has been abandoned or neglected.

words.ex: He led a dissolute life after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后过着放荡的生活。
words.en: If you describe someone as dissolute, you mean they behave in a way that is considered immoral because they do things such as drink or have sex too much.

words.ex: He still feels rancor toward his old boss.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然对他的前老板怀有怨恨。
words.en: A feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will.

words.tr:
v. 完成；使完美；圆房
adj. 完美的；至上的；圆满的
words.ex: He consummated the deal with a handshake.
words.ex_cn: 他用握手完成了这笔交易。
words.en: To consummate means to make something complete or perfect, often used in the context of a marriage or an agreement. It can also describe someone who is extremely skilled in a particular area.

words.tr: n. 警告；防止误解的说明；注意事项
words.ex: He gave me a warning, a caveat, before I signed the contract.
words.ex_cn: 我在签署合同之前，他给了我一个警告，一个注意事项。
words.en: A caveat is a warning of a specific limitation of something such as information or an agreement.

words.tr:
v. 磨碎；磨擦；（使）烦躁；发出磨擦声
n. 炉栅；炉箅
words.ex: The food was grated into small pieces.
words.ex_cn: 食物被擦成了小块。
