words.en: To grate means to reduce food to small shreds by rubbing it on a grater. It can also mean to make a harsh, scraping sound or to cause irritation or annoyance.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.tr:
n. 颈手枷
v. 给…上颈手枷；使惹人嘲笑；示众；公开批评
words.ex: The newspaper did not hesitate to pillory the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸毫不犹豫地公开谴责那位腐败的政客。
words.en: A pillory is a wooden framework with holes for the head and hands, in which offenders were formerly locked and exposed to public abuse or ridicule. As a verb, to pillory means to expose someone to public scorn, ridicule, or abuse.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.tr: v. 使夷为平地；彻底摧毁
words.ex: They will raze the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将把那座旧建筑夷为平地。
words.en: To raze a building, town, or forest means to completely destroy it, especially by knocking it down or burning it.

words.ex: He estranged his brother with harsh words.
words.ex_cn: 他用刻薄的话与兄弟疏远了。
words.en: If you estrange someone, especially a member of your family, you cause them to stop being friendly or close to you.

words.tr:
n. 熏香；熏香的烟
v. 使愤怒；激怒
words.ex: The smell of incense fills the room.
words.ex_cn: 香火的气味充满了房间。
words.en: Incense is a substance that is burned for its pleasant smell, often used in religious ceremonies. As a verb, to incense means to make someone very angry.

words.ex: His testimony proved the suspect was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他的证词证明了嫌疑人是无辜的。
words.en: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law.

words.ex: The ball has a convex surface.
words.ex_cn: 这个球有一个凸出的表面。
words.en: A convex surface curves outward in the middle.

words.tr: adj. 每日的；平凡的；平常的
words.ex: He drinks coffee every quotidian morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: Something that is quotidian occurs every day or is very common and ordinary.

words.ex: The riot broke out after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
words.en: A riot is a violent disturbance of the peace by a crowd.

words.tr: adj. 芬香的；特别美味的
words.ex: The scent of the ambrosial flowers filled the air.
words.ex_cn: 芬芳馥郁的花香弥漫在空气中。
words.en: Something that is ambrosial is extremely pleasant to taste or smell, often described as divine or heavenly.

words.tr: adj. 难以控制的；任性的；捉摸不定的
words.ex: The wayward child refused to listen to his parents.
words.ex_cn: 这个任性的孩子不肯听父母的话。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as wayward, you mean that they behave in a selfish, bad, or unpredictable way, and are difficult to control.

words.tr: v. （使）窒息而死；使呼吸困难；闷死
words.ex: The smoke is suffocating him.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾正在让他窒息。
words.en: To cause someone to die or to make it difficult for someone to breathe by preventing air from reaching the lungs.

words.ex: His rubicund complexion suggested good health.
words.ex_cn: 他红润的面色显示了良好的健康状况。
words.en: If someone has a rubicund face, they have a healthy red color in their cheeks.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.ex: He tried to bribe the officer with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱贿赂官员。
words.en: A bribe is a sum of money or something valuable that one person offers or gives to another in order to persuade them to do something, usually something dishonest.

words.tr: v. （使）回转；（使）侧滑n. 大量；许多v. 杀死；杀害；残害；宰杀；“slay”的过去式
words.ex: The car slewed around the corner.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在拐角处突然转向。
words.en: To kill someone or something in a violent way; to turn or slide violently or uncontrollably in a particular direction.

words.ex: He fell into a coma after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后陷入了昏迷。
words.en: A coma is a state of deep unconsciousness that lasts for a prolonged or indefinite period, caused especially by severe injury or illness.

words.ex: He abnegates his own needs for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他为了家人而放弃自己的需求。
words.en: If you abnegate something, you renounce or reject it.

words.ex: The house has a commodious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A commodious room or building is large and has a lot of space.

words.ex: He had a meager meal after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后吃了一顿很少的饭。
words.en: If you describe an amount or quantity of something as meager, you are critical of it because it is very small or not enough.

words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.tr:
adj. 引火的；燃烧的；纵火的；煽动的
n. 燃烧弹
words.ex: The incendiary device set the building on fire.
words.ex_cn: 这个引火装置把大楼点燃了。
words.en: An incendiary device is designed to cause fires. Incendiary remarks or actions are likely to cause anger or violence.

words.ex: He was known for being tightfisted with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他因对金钱的吝啬而闻名。
words.en: If you describe someone as tightfisted, you disapprove of them because they are unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.ex: The choir sang a paean of praise for the retiring principal.
words.ex_cn: 合唱团为即将退休的校长唱了一首赞歌。
words.en: A paean is a song of praise, joy, or triumph.

words.tr: n. 敏捷的回答；机智的回答
words.ex: The witty repartee between the two comedians kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 两位喜剧演员之间的机智对话让观众笑声不断。
words.en: A repartee is a quick, witty reply or a conversation full of such replies.

words.tr: v. 闪烁；发火花；焕发才智
words.ex: The diamonds on her necklace scintillated under the light.
words.ex_cn: 她项链上的钻石在灯光下闪闪发光。
words.en: To emit sparks or to sparkle; to twinkle; to be brilliant or lively in conversation or performance.

words.tr: adj. 不确切的；不精确的；
words.ex: His answer was imprecise and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不确切，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as imprecise, you mean that it is not stated or done accurately or clearly.

words.tr: n. 混乱；动荡；骚乱；恐慌
words.ex: The storm caused turmoil in the town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty.

words.ex: He earned the esteem of his colleagues through hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作赢得了同事们的尊重。
words.en: If you esteem someone or something, you respect or admire them.

words.tr:
v. 拙劣地做；搞砸
n. 搞糟了的事情；失误
words.ex: He bungled the simple task.
words.ex_cn: 他把简单的任务搞砸了。
words.en: To bungle something means to do it badly or clumsily, often resulting in failure or mistakes.

words.ex: The scrappy room was full of clothes and toys on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 这个不整洁的房间里到处都是衣服和玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as scrappy, you mean that they are determined and unwilling to give up, even in a difficult situation.

words.tr: v. 使…情绪低落；使沮丧
words.ex: The bad news dejected him.
words.ex_cn: 坏消息使他沮丧。
words.en: If you are dejected, you feel miserable or unhappy, especially because you have just been disappointed by something.

words.tr:
adj. （《圣经》中所说的大洪水前的）古老的；过时的
n.  年迈的人；不合时宜的人
words.ex: He uses an antediluvian typewriter to write letters.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台远古的打字机写信。
words.en: Belonging to the time before the biblical Flood; very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.tr: adj. 需要久坐的；惯于久坐不动的；不爱活动的；
words.ex: His sedentary job makes him sit all day.
words.ex_cn: 他的久坐工作让他整天坐着。
words.en: Someone who has a sedentary lifestyle or job sits down a lot of the time and does not take much exercise.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.tr: n. 权威人士；专家；评论员
words.ex: The pundit said the team will win tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这位专家说球队明天会赢。
words.en: A pundit is a person who knows a lot about a particular subject and is often asked to give their opinions to the public.

words.tr: n. 重型卡车；不可抗拒的强大力量；无法控制的强大机构；使人盲目牺牲（或崇拜）的事物
words.ex: The juggernaut rolled down the highway, carrying heavy cargo.
words.ex_cn: 这辆重型卡车沿着高速公路行驶，载着沉重的货物。
words.en: A juggernaut is something or someone that is extremely large, powerful, and unstoppable.

words.tr: adj. 没有回报的；无报酬的；有仇未报的；单方面的
words.ex: She suffered from unrequited love for many years.
words.ex_cn: 多年来，她一直承受着单恋之苦。
words.en: If you say that something such as love or affection is unrequited, you mean that it is not returned by the person it is directed towards.

words.tr: adj. 装作圣洁的；伪善的
words.ex: He gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一番关于诚实的伪善演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as sanctimonious, you disapprove of them because you think that they are trying to appear morally better than other people.

words.ex: The car took a precipitous turn on the mountain road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在山路上急转弯。
words.en: A precipitous slope or cliff is very steep and often dangerous.

words.tr: n. 精神欢快；兴高采烈
words.ex: He felt euphoria after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后感到无比兴奋。
words.en: A feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.ex: He felt impuissance after the failure.
words.ex_cn: 失败后，他感到无能为力。
words.en: The state or condition of being powerless or lacking strength.

words.ex: The machine can perforate the paper quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器可以快速地在纸上打孔。
words.en: To make a hole or holes through something, especially by piercing or drilling.

words.ex: He resorted to chicanery to win the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠狡辩赢得了争论。
words.en: The use of trickery to achieve a political, financial, or legal purpose.

words.ex: He made a gaffe when he called the boss by the wrong name.
words.ex_cn: 他叫错老板的名字，犯了个错误。
words.en: A gaffe is a mistake that a person makes in public, especially something embarrassing that they say or do.

words.tr: adj. 观察力敏锐的；谨慎遵守的；
words.ex: She is observant and notices small details.
words.ex_cn: 她观察力敏锐，能注意到细小的细节。
words.en: Someone who is observant pays close attention to things and notices more about them than most people do.

words.ex: Her motto is 'Never give up.'
words.ex_cn: 她的座右铭是‘永不放弃’。
words.en: A motto is a short sentence or phrase that expresses a rule for sensible behavior, especially a way of behaving in a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 无知觉的；无生命力的
words.ex: The statue remained insentient, unaffected by the passing years.
words.ex_cn: 雕像依旧无知觉，不受岁月流逝的影响。
words.en: Lacking consciousness or the ability to perceive.

words.tr: adj. 同等的；相等的；相当于
words.ex: Lying is tantamount to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎等于欺骗。
words.en: If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

words.ex: He gave a dolorous look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出悲伤的表情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or appearance as dolorous, you mean that it is very sad and depressing.

words.ex: The story was a complete canard, spread by those with vested interests.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事完全是一个谣言，是由那些有既得利益的人散布的。
words.en: A canard is a false or baseless story or piece of information, especially one that is deliberately misleading.

words.ex: He contorts his face to make the kids laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他扭曲面部表情来逗孩子们笑。
words.en: If someone's face or body contorts or is contorted, it moves into an unnatural and unattractive shape or position.

words.ex: They made a concerted effort to clean the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们共同努力清理了公园。
words.en: A concerted action or effort is done by several people or groups working together.

words.tr:
v. 臆测；猜想
n. 臆测；猜度
words.ex: He surmises that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you surmise that something is true, you guess it from the available evidence, although you do not know for certain.

words.tr: v. 迅速生长；急速增长
words.ex: The flowers burgeon in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，花朵绽放。
words.en: To grow or develop quickly; to flourish.

words.ex: He embezzled money from his company.
words.ex_cn: 他从公司贪污了钱。
words.en: To embezzle means to steal or misappropriate money placed in one's trust or belonging to one's employer.

words.tr:
n. 屏幕；屏风；掩蔽物；
v. 筛查；掩蔽；
words.ex: The movie is playing on the screen.
words.ex_cn: 电影正在屏幕上播放。
words.en: A screen is a flat surface on which pictures or words are shown, such as the one on a television or computer. It can also refer to a partition used to divide or protect an area. As a verb, to screen means to examine something in order to decide whether it is suitable for a particular purpose, or to protect someone or something from something harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: He wants to emigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.

words.tr:
v. 使翘棱；使扭曲变形
n. 弯曲；歪曲
words.ex: The heat will warp the metal.
words.ex_cn: 热量会使金属变形。
words.en: To warp is to bend or twist something out of its natural shape, often as a result of heat or moisture. It can also refer to the state of being bent or twisted.

words.ex: His pusillanimous behavior in the face of danger was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前的懦弱行为令人失望。
words.en: If you say that someone is pusillanimous, you mean that they are timid or afraid, especially in a way that you find irritating or disappointing.

words.tr:
v. 意思；导致；打算；
n. 平均数；
adj. 低劣；平均；
words.ex: What does this word mean?
words.ex_cn: 这个词是什么意思？
words.en: If you want to know what a word, a sentence, or an expression means, you want to know what it refers to or what its significance is.

words.ex: He gave a sincere apology.
words.ex_cn: 他真诚地道歉了。
words.en: If you say that someone is sincere, you approve of them because they really mean the things they say.

words.ex: He tried to debase the coin with cheap metal.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用廉价金属贬低硬币的价值。
words.en: To debase something means to reduce its value or quality.

words.tr: n. 三段论法；推论法；演绎
words.ex: He used a syllogism to prove his point.
words.ex_cn: 他用三段论来证明他的观点。
words.en: A syllogism is a form of reasoning in which a conclusion is drawn from two given or assumed propositions (premises); a common or middle term is present in the two premises but not in the conclusion, which is deduced from the premises.

words.tr:
adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极端的；过分的
v. 变高尚；升华
n. 庄严；崇高；顶点
words.ex: The view from the mountain is sublime.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色是壮丽的。
words.en: If you describe something as sublime, you mean that it has a wonderful quality that affects you deeply.

words.ex: His hubris made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: Hubris is excessive pride or self-confidence, often leading to downfall or failure.

words.ex: He perambulates through the park every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上在公园里散步。
words.en: To walk or travel through a place, especially for pleasure and in a leisurely way.

words.tr: v. 使焦虑；使不安；扰乱
words.ex: The noise perturbs the baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让婴儿不安。
words.en: If something perturbs you, it makes you feel anxious or worried.

words.tr:
n. 补锅匠
v. 小修；小补；摆弄
words.ex: He is a tinker who fixes old pots and pans.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名补锅匠，修理旧锅旧盆。
words.en: If you tinker with something, you make some small changes to it in an attempt to improve it or repair it.

words.tr: n. 大胆的尝试；精湛的技艺
words.ex: Her bravura performance left the audience in awe.
words.ex_cn: 她精湛的表演让观众惊叹不已。
words.en: A bravura performance is one that is very skillful and exciting.

words.ex: He carved the meat with a sharp knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用一把锋利的刀切开了肉。
words.en: To carve means to cut into a hard material in order to produce an object, design, or inscription.

words.ex: He is an earnest student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个认真的学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you are earnest about something, you are serious about it and your intentions are honest and sincere.

words.ex: He asked for her consent before starting the project.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始这个项目之前征求了她的同意。
words.en: Consent is permission for something to happen or agreement to do something.

words.ex: The needy family received food from the charity.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的家庭从慈善机构收到了食物。
words.en: Needy people do not have enough food, medicine, or clothing, or adequate houses.

words.tr: adj. 势利的；谄上欺下的
words.ex: He is snobbish and ignores people who are not rich.
words.ex_cn: 他很势利，不理睬不富有的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as snobbish, you disapprove of them because they are too proud of their social status, intelligence, or taste.

words.ex: The situation required an exigent response.
words.ex_cn: 这种情况需要紧急应对。
words.en: Requiring immediate action or attention; urgent.

words.ex: The speech was a panegyric to the retiring chairman.
words.ex_cn: 这场演讲是对即将退休的主席的赞颂。
words.en: A panegyric is a formal public speech, or written verse, delivered in high praise of a person or thing, a eulogy.

words.ex: The downpour soaked everyone outside.
words.ex_cn: 暴雨把外面的每个人都淋湿了。
words.en: A downpour is a sudden and unexpected heavy fall of rain.

words.tr: adj. 可触摸的；实际的；有形的；确凿的；
words.ex: The statue is tangible and can be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像可以触摸，是实实在在的。
words.en: Something that is tangible is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.tr: n. 犹豫；踌躇；迟疑不决
words.ex: Her hesitance to commit was evident in her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 她眼中的犹豫表明了她不愿承诺。
words.en: Hesitance is the state or quality of being hesitant, which means to be slow to act, speak, or decide because of uncertainty or reluctance.

words.tr:
n. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
v. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
words.ex: The general countermanded the order to attack.
words.ex_cn: 将军取消了进攻的命令。
words.en: If you countermand an order, you cancel it, usually by giving a different order.

words.ex: He likes to dabble in various hobbies.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢涉猎各种爱好。
words.en: If you dabble in something, you take part in it but not very seriously.

words.ex: The clay is malleable and easy to shape.
words.ex_cn: 这种黏土是可塑的，容易塑形。
words.en: If you say that someone is malleable, you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.

words.tr: n. 嘲笑；愚弄；被嘲笑的对象
words.ex: He laughed in mockery of her mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他嘲笑她的错误。
words.en: Mockery is the act of mocking someone or something or the state of being mocked.

words.ex: He sang a mournful song at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他在葬礼上唱了一首悲伤的歌。
words.en: If you are mournful, you are very sad.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.tr:
v. 摇摆；摇动
n. 摇摆；爱说笑的人
words.ex: The dog wagged its tail happily.
words.ex_cn: 狗开心地摇着尾巴。
words.en: If a dog wags its tail, it moves its tail from side to side, often because it is happy or excited.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.tr: n. 乌合之众；下等人；聚众的暴民
words.ex: The police had to disperse the rabble before the situation got out of hand.
words.ex_cn: 警察不得不在情况失控之前驱散暴民。
words.en: A rabble is a disorganized or disorderly crowd of people.

words.tr: n. 摧毁；拆毁；拆除；大败；
words.ex: The demolition of the old building started last week.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧楼的拆除上周开始了。
words.en: The act of demolishing something, especially a building.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；命中注定的；决定命运的；预言性的
words.ex: It was a fateful day when he met her.
words.ex_cn: 那是他遇见她的命运般的一天。
words.en: If you describe an event or action as fateful, you mean that it has very important and often bad effects on the future.

words.ex: He looked at the lie with contempt.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.

words.tr: n. 困境；窘境；困惑之境；进退两难
words.ex: He is in a quandary about what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他对于该做什么感到困惑。
words.en: A situation in which you are unsure or confused about what to do.

words.ex: He achieved mastery of the piano after ten years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 他经过十年的练习，熟练掌握了钢琴。
words.en: If you show mastery of a particular skill or language, you show that you have learned or understood it completely and have no difficulty using it.

words.tr:
adj. 吸引人的；引人入胜的
v. （用铆钉）固定；吸引住；“rivet”的现在分词
words.ex: The movie was riveting from start to finish.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影从头到尾都扣人心弦。
words.en: If you describe something as riveting, you mean that it is extremely interesting and exciting, and that it holds your attention completely.

words.tr:
adj. 刺耳的；不和谐的；冲突的
v. （使）震动；令人不快；冲突；不一致；“jar”的现在分词
words.ex: The loud music was jarring to her ears.
words.ex_cn: 那刺耳的音乐让她感到不适。
words.en: If you describe something as jarring, you mean that it has a harsh and unpleasant effect, especially because it seems out of place.

words.ex: The government's policy aimed to deracinate the rebel group.
words.ex_cn: 政府的政策旨在根除叛乱组织。
words.en: To deracinate someone or something means to remove them from their natural environment or culture, especially in a way that causes them to lose their identity or characteristics.

words.ex: The game simulates real traffic conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏模拟了真实的交通状况。
words.en: To simulate is to create a model or representation of a situation, process, or system for the purpose of study, analysis, or training. It involves imitating the conditions of a real event or environment to understand its effects or to practice responses to it.

words.tr: v. 确定无罪；免除（罪责）
words.ex: The new evidence helped to exonerate him.
words.ex_cn: 新的证据帮助他洗清了罪名。
words.en: If someone is exonerated, they are proved to be not guilty of a crime or responsible for something bad that happened.

words.ex: He felt remorse after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友撒谎后感到后悔。
words.en: Remorse is a strong feeling of sadness and regret about something wrong that you have done.

words.ex: The plan went awry when the rain started.
words.ex_cn: 当雨下起来时，计划就出差错了。
words.en: If something goes awry, it does not happen in the way that was planned.

words.tr:
v. （风）狂吹；咆哮；恫吓；咄咄逼人
n. 狂风声；咆哮；吓唬；夸口
words.ex: The wind blustered through the trees all night.
words.ex_cn: 风整晚狂吹着穿过树木。
words.en: If you say that someone is blustering, you mean that they are speaking aggressively but without authority, often because they are angry or offended.

words.tr: adj. 轻松活泼的；得意洋洋的；自信满满的
words.ex: He walked with a jaunty step, clearly pleased with himself.
words.ex_cn: 他步伐轻快，显然对自己感到很满意。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jaunty, you mean that they are full of confidence and energy.

words.tr: adj. 俗丽而不值钱的；花里胡哨的
words.ex: She wore a tawdry dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着一件俗丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as tawdry, you mean that it is showy and bright but of very poor quality.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.tr: adj. 极端或过分热情的
words.ex: His perfervid speech inspired the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他那热情洋溢的演讲激励了群众。
words.en: Having or showing intense and fervent feeling or enthusiasm.

words.tr:
v. 畏缩不前；犹豫；妨碍
n. 阻碍，妨碍
words.ex: He balks at paying high prices.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意支付高价。
words.en: If you balk at something, you hesitate to do it or agree to it, often because it is unpleasant or difficult.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.tr: v. 制定（法律）；通过（法律）；扮演（角色）
words.ex: The government will enact a new law next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将颁布一项新法律。
words.en: To enact a law or rule means to make it official by passing it through a legislative body.

words.ex: He etches a design on the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他在玻璃上刻了一个图案。
words.en: To etch means to cut into a surface, especially metal or glass, using acid or a sharp tool, in order to create a design or pattern.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.ex: Life is full of vicissitude.
words.ex_cn: 生活充满起伏。
words.en: A change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome or unpleasant.

words.ex: The government is working to reduce illiteracy in rural areas.
words.ex_cn: 政府正在努力减少农村地区的文盲。
words.en: Illiteracy is the condition of being unable to read and write.

words.tr:
adj. 原来的；有创造性的；原版的；新颖的；
n. 原件；原稿；
words.ex: This is the original book I bought last year.
words.ex_cn: 这是我去年买的那本原版书。
words.en: An original piece of writing or music was written recently and has not been published or performed before.

words.tr:
v. 突然转向；改变方向
n. 转向
words.ex: He swerved to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 他为了避开狗而转向。
words.en: If a vehicle or other moving thing swerves, it suddenly changes direction, often in order to avoid hitting something.

words.tr: v. 幸灾乐祸；沾沾自喜；满足地看
words.ex: He gloats when his rival loses the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的对手输掉比赛时，他幸灾乐祸。
words.en: To gloat means to observe or think about something with triumphant and often malicious satisfaction, gratification, or delight.

words.ex: The company paid indemnity for the damaged car.
words.ex_cn: 公司为损坏的汽车支付了保险赔偿。
words.en: If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss, especially in the form of a legal agreement.

words.tr: adj. 非常亮的；浓艳的；苍白的；血红的；可怕的；（故意地）骇人听闻的
words.ex: The lurid neon signs lit up the night street.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的霓虹灯照亮了夜晚的街道。
words.en: If you say that something is lurid, you are critical of it because it involves a lot of violence, sex, or shocking detail.

words.tr:
v. 后悔；懊悔
n. 懊悔；后悔；芸香
words.ex: He rue the decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他后悔辞去工作的决定。
words.en: A feeling of deep regret or remorse for a past action or mistake.

words.tr: n. 衬垫； v. “pad”的现在分词；
words.ex: The box has foam padding to protect the glass.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子有泡沫衬垫来保护玻璃。
words.en: Padding is soft material which is put on something or inside it in order to make it less hard, to protect it, or to give it a different shape.

words.ex: He is diligent in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都很勤奋地做作业。
words.en: Someone who is diligent works hard and is careful and thorough.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: The judge will absolve him of all charges.
words.ex_cn: 法官将免除他所有的罪名。
words.en: If someone is absolved of blame, responsibility, or a sin, they are formally forgiven for it or declared free from it.

words.ex: He couldn't budge the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他无法让那个重箱子稍微移动一下。
words.en: If someone will not budge on a matter, or if nothing budges them, they refuse to change their mind or to come to an agreement.

words.tr:
n. 划分；隔离物；分割
v. 分开；隔开
words.ex: The partition of the room made it more private.
words.ex_cn: 房间的隔断让它更私密了。
words.en: A partition is a wall, screen, or divider that separates one part of a room, vehicle, or other space from another.

words.tr:
n. 蓄意破坏
v. 蓄意破坏；暗中破坏
words.ex: He tried to sabotage the project.
words.ex_cn: 他试图破坏这个项目。
words.en: Sabotage is the act of deliberately destroying, damaging, or obstructing something, especially for political or military advantage.

words.ex: The parrot can say hello.
words.ex_cn: 这只鹦鹉会说你好。
words.en: A parrot is a tropical bird with a curved beak and brightly colored feathers. Parrots are often kept as pets because they can be taught to copy human speech.

words.tr:
adj. 狂热入迷的；盲信的
n. 狂热者；盲信者
words.ex: He is a fanatic fan of soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他对足球狂热入迷。
words.en: A fanatic is a person who is very enthusiastic about and devoted to a particular activity, cause, or belief, often to an extreme degree.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.tr:
v. 乱写；乱画；涂鸦
n. 乱画；乱写；涂鸦
words.ex: He doodled on his notebook during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时在笔记本上乱画。
words.en: If you doodle, you draw small, simple pictures or patterns on a piece of paper, often while you are thinking about something else.

words.ex: The dancer's movements were mesmeric.
words.ex_cn: 舞者的动作令人着迷。
words.en: Having the power to hold someone's attention or interest in a way that is almost magical, or relating to hypnosis.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.tr: v. 厚厚地覆盖；使…窒息；闷死
words.ex: He tried to smother the fire with a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用毯子把火闷灭。
words.en: To smother someone or something means to kill them by covering their face so that they cannot breathe, or to put out a fire by covering it.

words.ex: The synergic team worked well together.
words.ex_cn: 这个协作的团队合作得很好。
words.en: Involving interaction or cooperation between two or more organizations, substances, or other agents to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their separate effects.

words.tr:
v. 无所事事；闲荡
adj. 懈怠的；闲散的；不做事的
words.ex: He idles away the whole afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他整个下午都无所事事。
words.en: If you describe someone as idle, you mean they are not doing anything or they are not working hard.

words.tr:
v. 咆哮；吼叫；（使）缠结
n. 咆哮（声）；缠结
words.ex: The dog snarls at strangers.
words.ex_cn: 狗对陌生人咆哮。
words.en: If an animal snarls, it makes a fierce, rough noise in its throat, usually to show anger.

words.ex: His preoccupation with video games made him ignore his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的全神贯注让他忽略了作业。
words.en: If you have a preoccupation with something or someone, you think or worry about them very often and they are the main focus of your attention.

words.ex: He had a dour expression on his face.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上带着严厉的表情。
words.en: If you describe someone as dour, you mean they are very serious and unfriendly.

words.ex: The floor is slippery after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 下雨后地板很滑。
words.en: Something that is slippery is smooth, wet, or oily and is therefore difficult to walk on or to hold.

words.ex: The tyrant ruled the country with fear.
words.ex_cn: 暴君用恐惧统治国家。
words.en: A tyrant is a ruler who has complete power in a country and uses it in a cruel and unfair way.

words.tr:
n. 马鞍；鞍座
v. 给（马）装鞍
words.ex: The boy rode on a saddle on the horse.
words.ex_cn: 男孩骑在马的马鞍上。
words.en: A saddle is a seat for a rider on the back of a horse or other animal, or a similar seat on a bicycle or motorcycle. It can also refer to the act of putting a saddle on a horse or to burden someone with a responsibility.

words.tr: v. 攻击；困扰；抨击；袭击
words.ex: The storm assailed the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴袭击了这个小村庄。
words.en: If someone assails you, they attack you violently, either physically or with words.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；失误
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；失误；跌跌撞撞地走
words.ex: He made a big blunder in the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中犯了一个大错误。
words.en: A blunder is a stupid or careless mistake.

words.ex: His bonhomie made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 他的温和让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: A cheerful and friendly manner; geniality.

words.ex: His persistence helped him pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚持让他通过了考试。
words.en: Persistence is the determination to do something even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: The dog cowers when the thunder sounds.
words.ex_cn: 当雷声响起时，狗会蜷缩起来。
words.en: To crouch down in fear.

words.tr:
v. 加酵母；使发酵；影响
n. 酵素；酵母；潜移默化的影响
words.ex: She uses yeast to leaven the bread.
words.ex_cn: 她用酵母使面包发酵。
words.en: Leaven is a substance, typically yeast, that is used in dough to make it rise. It can also refer to something that modifies or lightens a situation or atmosphere.

words.tr: adj. 无思虑的；考虑不周的
words.ex: His incogitant remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他无心的话语伤了她的感情。
words.en: Lacking thought or consideration; thoughtless.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.ex: The dark clouds forebode a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something forebodes a future event, it suggests that it is going to happen.

words.tr: n. 冗长无聊的废话；繁琐的程序；一连串的无聊举动
words.ex: He went on a rigmarole about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他滔滔不绝地讲述他的童年。
words.en: A rigmarole is a long and complicated process that seems unnecessary and is often annoying.

words.ex: She bought a new garment for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件新衣服。
words.en: A garment is a piece of clothing; used especially in contexts where you are talking about the manufacture or sale of clothes.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；无礼的；侮慢的
words.ex: The insolent boy talked back to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个无礼的男孩顶撞了老师。
words.en: If you say that someone is insolent, you mean they are rude and do not show respect for people in positions of authority.

words.tr: adj. 半熟的；未完成的；不完整的
words.ex: His half-baked idea failed at once.
words.ex_cn: 他那不成熟的想法立刻失败了。
words.en: If you describe an idea or plan as half-baked, you mean that it has not been properly thought out, and so is stupid or impractical.

words.tr:
adj. 不锋利的；耿直的
v. 使变钝
words.ex: The knife is blunt and cannot cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀不锋利，切不动纸。
words.en: If you are blunt, you say exactly what you think without trying to be polite.

words.tr: v. 使无效；使显得愚蠢
words.ex: The boring meeting stultifies his creativity.
words.ex_cn: 这个无聊的会议扼杀了他的创造力。
words.en: To stultify someone or something means to cause them to appear foolish or to be ineffective.

words.tr: adj. 被虫蛀的；破旧的；过时的
words.ex: The moth-eaten coat looked out of place in the modern setting.
words.ex_cn: 这件虫蛀的外套在现代环境中显得格格不入。
words.en: Something that is moth-eaten is old and in bad condition, often because it has been eaten by moths or because it is very old and has not been looked after well.

words.tr:
v. 冲洗；灌洗；涮；大口喝
n. 涮；冲洗；痛饮；泔水
words.ex: He drank the swill from the old bucket.
words.ex_cn: 他喝掉了旧桶里的脏水。
words.en: To drink something quickly and in large amounts, or to wash something by pouring large amounts of water over or through it.

words.tr:
adj. 怪诞的；丑陋奇异的；奇形怪状的
n. 奇形怪状的东西；奇异风格
words.ex: The painting showed a grotesque face with twisted eyes.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画上有一个扭曲眼睛的怪诞面孔。
words.en: If you say that something is grotesque, you mean that it is extremely unattractive, exaggerated, and often shocking or disturbing.

words.tr: adj. 斜躺的；斜靠的；侧卧的
words.ex: The old man sat in a recumbent chair.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人坐在一张躺椅上。
words.en: A recumbent position or posture is one in which a person is lying down or leaning back in a relaxed manner.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.ex: The foreword explains why the book was written.
words.ex_cn: 序言解释了这本书为何被撰写。
words.en: A foreword is a short introduction at the beginning of a book, usually written by someone other than the author.

words.tr:
n. 药膏；软膏；油膏
v. 使良心得到宽慰；减轻内疚感
words.ex: He put a salve on his cut to help it heal.
words.ex_cn: 他在伤口上涂了药膏以帮助愈合。
words.en: A salve is a soothing ointment used to promote healing of the skin or as a remedy for a sore or ailment.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: It was an utter mistake.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个完全的错误。
words.en: To say something or to make a sound with your voice; complete or absolute.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: She wrote a letter to condole with him on his loss.
words.ex_cn: 她写了一封信，对他的损失表示慰问。
words.en: To express sympathy or sorrow for someone who has experienced a misfortune or loss.

words.ex: He had the effrontery to lie to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他竟敢对老师撒谎。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as effrontery, you are emphasizing that it is very rude or disrespectful.

words.tr:
n. 凝块；泥团；密集的一群
v. 凝结成块
words.ex: The blood began to clot after the cut.
words.ex_cn: 伤口流血后开始凝固。
words.en: A clot is a sticky lump that forms when blood dries up or becomes thick. If blood clots, it becomes thick and forms a lump.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.ex: She tried to browbeat him into submission.
words.ex_cn: 她试图恫吓他屈服。
words.en: To intimidate or bully someone into doing something, especially by using threats or aggressive behavior.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.ex: He answered the question with tact.
words.ex_cn: 他机智地回答了这个问题。
words.en: If you describe what someone says or does as tact, you mean that it is polite, considerate, and shows an understanding of other people's feelings.

words.tr: adj. 不机智的；不机敏的；不老练的；不圆滑的；不乖巧的
words.ex: He was tactless when he criticized her in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前批评她，显得很不妥当。
words.en: If you describe someone as tactless, you think what they say or do is likely to offend other people.

words.tr: n. 堕落的人；不道德的人
words.ex: The townspeople shunned the reprobate, fearing his influence.
words.ex_cn: 镇上的人们都避开那个堕落的人，害怕他的影响。
words.en: A reprobate is a person who behaves in a way that is morally wrong and who shows no regret or shame for their actions.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: The new mayor was accused of cronyism in his appointments.
words.ex_cn: 新市长在任命上被指控有任人唯亲的行为。
words.en: Cronyism is the practice of appointing friends and associates to positions of authority, without proper regard to their qualifications.

words.tr: adj. 可估量的；值得尊重的
words.ex: The cost of the project is estimable with current data.
words.ex_cn: 根据当前数据，这个项目的成本是可以估量的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as estimable, you mean that they deserve admiration because they are extremely good or have a very good quality.

words.tr:
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措
n. 迷惑；困惑；为难
words.ex: The tricky question nonplused the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个棘手的问题让老师不知所措。
words.en: To cause to be at a loss as to what to say, think, or do; perplex.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.ex: He accepted the job because of the financial inducement.
words.ex_cn: 他因为经济诱因接受了这份工作。
words.en: Something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.tr: v. 安抚；讨好；使息怒；调和
words.ex: He tried to conciliate his angry neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他试图安抚他生气的邻居。
words.en: If you conciliate someone, you try to end a disagreement with them by doing or saying things that will make them less angry or more friendly.

words.ex: He made an unwonted silence during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上出乎意料地保持了沉默。
words.en: Not usual or common; unusual.

words.tr:
v. 润饰；修整
n. 润饰；修整
words.ex: The photographer spent hours retouching the photo to remove blemishes.
words.ex_cn: 摄影师花了几个小时修整照片以去除瑕疵。
words.en: To retouch a photograph or a piece of artwork means to improve its appearance by making small changes or corrections.

words.ex: The yokel laughed at the city lights.
words.ex_cn: 这个乡下人对城市灯光笑了。
words.en: A yokel is an uneducated and unsophisticated person from the countryside.

words.ex: The lamp illuminate the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: To illuminate something means to shine light on it and to make it brighter and more visible.

words.ex: The sponge is porous and absorbs water easily.
words.ex_cn: 海绵是多孔的，容易吸水。
words.en: If something is porous, it has a lot of tiny holes in it that allow water or air to pass through slowly.

words.ex: The prisoners suffered from sleep deprivation.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯们因睡眠剥夺而受苦。
words.en: Deprivation is the lack or denial of something considered to be a necessity.

words.ex: The milk is frothy after being steamed.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶经过蒸汽处理后变得泡沫丰富。
words.en: Frothy describes something that is full of or covered with a mass of small bubbles, or something that is light and entertaining but not serious.

words.tr:
n. 缝线；缝合处
v. 缝合（伤口）
words.ex: The doctor used a suture to close the wound.
words.ex_cn: 医生用缝合线缝合了伤口。
words.en: A suture is a stitch or row of stitches holding together the edges of a wound or surgical incision.

words.ex: He withdrew $100 from the ATM.
words.ex_cn: 他从自动取款机里提取了100美元。
words.en: If you withdraw something from a place, you remove it or take it away.

words.ex: He wore a big grin after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后露出了灿烂的咧嘴笑容。
words.en: If you grin, you smile broadly, usually showing your teeth.

words.ex: He spoke a soliloquy alone on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他独自在舞台上说了一段独白。
words.en: A soliloquy is a speech in a play in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud, often when they are alone on stage.

words.ex: The land is arable and good for growing wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这块地是可耕的，适合种植小麦。
words.en: Arable land is land that is suitable for growing crops.

words.tr: adj. 轻佻的；不可靠的；易惊慌的
words.ex: The horse is skittish around loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马对大声响很敏感。
words.en: If you describe a person or animal as skittish, you mean they are easily frightened or nervous.

words.tr:
v. （因发言冗长）妨碍（会议的进程）
n. （议会中为拖延表决的）冗长演说
words.ex: The senator used a filibuster to delay the vote on the bill.
words.ex_cn: 参议员使用阻挠议事行动来拖延对该法案的投票。
words.en: A filibuster is a tactic used in a legislative assembly to prevent a measure from being brought to a vote. It is most commonly associated with the U.S. Senate, where a senator or a group of senators may extend debate on a proposal indefinitely to delay or entirely prevent a decision on it.

words.ex: The line touches the circle at one point and is a tangent.
words.ex_cn: 这条线与圆在一个点相切，是一条切线。
words.en: A tangent is a straight line or plane that touches a curve or curved surface at a point, but if extended does not cross it at that point. In a more general sense, it can also refer to a sudden digression or change of course.

words.tr: n. 小配角；小品文；浮雕宝石
words.ex: She appeared in a cameo role in the film.
words.ex_cn: 她在电影中扮演了一个配角。
words.en: A cameo is a small but noticeable part in a film or play, often played by a famous actor or actress. It can also refer to a piece of jewelry consisting of a raised design on a background of a different color.

words.ex: His smile evinces joy.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑流露出快乐。
words.en: To show clearly that you have a particular quality, feeling, or ability.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.ex: The ground began to subside after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，地面开始下陷。
words.en: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

words.tr: n. 接穗，幼枝；（尤指富家）子孙
words.ex: The scion of the family now runs the business.
words.ex_cn: 这个家族的后代现在经营着这家企业。
words.en: A scion is a descendent or heir, especially of a wealthy, aristocratic, or influential family.

words.tr: v. 惠顾；资助；屈尊俯就
words.ex: He often patronizes the local bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他经常光顾这家本地面包店。
words.en: If someone patronizes you, they speak or behave towards you in a way which seems friendly, but which shows that they think they are superior to you in some way.

words.tr: adj. 不动声色的；无动于衷的；不易激动的
words.ex: He remained stolid in the face of adversity.
words.ex_cn: 面对逆境，他依然冷漠。
words.en: If you describe someone as stolid, you mean that they do not show much emotion or are not very exciting or interesting.

words.ex: After running for an hour, he felt fatigue.
words.ex_cn: 跑了一个小时后，他感到疲乏。
words.en: A feeling of extreme physical or mental tiredness.

words.tr:
n. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
v. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
words.ex: The boat made a sudden lurch to the left.
words.ex_cn: 船突然向左倾斜。
words.en: If you lurch, you move suddenly and uncontrollably in one direction.

words.ex: She macerated the fruit in wine overnight.
words.ex_cn: 她把水果在酒中浸泡了一整夜。
words.en: To macerate something means to soften it, or to cause it to break down, by soaking it in a liquid.

words.ex: He tried to agitate the workers to strike.
words.ex_cn: 他试图鼓动工人罢工。
words.en: If you agitate something, you stir it up or shake it. If something agitates you, it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.tr: v. 猛烈抨击；痛骂；激烈反对
words.ex: He often inveighs against the corruption in the government.
words.ex_cn: 他经常猛烈抨击政府中的腐败现象。
words.en: If you inveigh against something, you criticize it strongly.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.ex: The smell of food whetted his appetite.
words.ex_cn: 食物的香味刺激了他的食欲。
words.en: To whet something means to make it sharper or more intense.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.tr:
n. 膨胀；凸出部分；暴涨
v. 膨胀；凸出；急增
words.ex: The balloon begins to bulge when filled with air.
words.ex_cn: 气球充气时开始鼓起来。
words.en: If something bulges, it sticks out or swells in a rounded shape.

words.ex: He revised his answer to make it correct.
words.ex_cn: 他修正了他的答案，使其正确。
words.en: To revise something means to alter or amend it, especially in order to correct or improve it.

words.ex: The treaty established amity between the two nations.
words.ex_cn: 该条约确立了两国之间的友好关系。
words.en: A friendly relationship between people or countries.

words.ex: This rule is applicable to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If something is applicable to a particular situation, it is relevant or suitable for that situation.

words.ex: The court's decision led to the nullification of the contract.
words.ex_cn: 法院的裁决导致合同的无效。
words.en: The act of making something legally null and void; the state of being nullified.

words.tr:
n. 人群；一大群；众多
v. 群集；挤满；涌进
words.ex: A throng of people waited outside the store.
words.ex_cn: 一大群人站在商店外面等候。
words.en: A large, densely packed crowd of people or animals.

words.ex: She is assertive when she speaks up for her rights.
words.ex_cn: 当她为自己权利发声时，表现得坚定自信。
words.en: Someone who is assertive behaves confidently and is not frightened to say what they want or believe.

words.tr:
n. 窥探；杠杆；爱打探的人
v. 打听；窥探；用杠杆撬开
words.ex: His pry into my private messages made me angry.
words.ex_cn: 他窥探我的私信让我很生气。
words.en: To try to find out private information about someone or something in a way that is annoying or rude.

words.ex: He speaks fluent English.
words.ex_cn: 他讲一口流利的英语。
words.en: If someone is fluent in a particular language, they can speak it easily and correctly.

words.tr: adj. 恶魔似的；残忍的；穷凶极恶的
words.ex: The plot of the novel is filled with diabolic twists and turns.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说的情节充满了魔鬼般的曲折变化。
words.en: If you describe something as diabolic, you are emphasizing that it is evil, cruel, or very bad.

words.ex: He got a driver's license last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周拿到了驾照。
words.en: A license is an official document which gives you permission to do, use, or own something.

words.tr:
v. （使）突然移动；快速投掷；
n. 镖；
words.ex: The cat darted across the room.
words.ex_cn: 猫突然冲过房间。
words.en: A dart is a small, narrow object with a sharp point which can be thrown or shot. It can also mean to move suddenly and quickly in a particular direction.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.ex: He tried to usurp the throne from his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从他兄弟手中篡夺王位。
words.en: If you say that someone usurps a job, role, title, or position, they take it from someone when they have no right to do this.

words.ex: She bedecks her room with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用鲜花装饰她的房间。
words.en: To decorate or adorn something, often in a showy or elaborate manner.

words.tr:
n. V字形刻痕；等级；切口
v. 赢得；刻凹痕
words.ex: He made a notch on the stick to count days.
words.ex_cn: 他在木棍上刻了一个刻痕来计数天数。
words.en: A notch is a small cut or indentation in a surface. It can also refer to a level or degree in a scale or a narrow pass between mountains.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；好争吵的；活跃的
words.ex: She was a feisty woman who never backed down from a challenge.
words.ex_cn: 她是个坚强的女人，从不向挑战低头。
words.en: If you describe someone as feisty, you mean that they are tough, independent, and spirited, often willing to argue or fight.

words.tr:
n. 顽固分子
adj. 顽固的
words.ex: He is a diehard fan of soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他是个狂热的足球迷。
words.en: A diehard is someone who is very strongly opposed to change and new ideas, and refuses to accept them, often in a way that seems unreasonable.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.ex: The rope constringe around the box.
words.ex_cn: 绳子紧紧缠绕在盒子上。
words.en: To make or become narrower or tighter by squeezing or pressing.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.ex: He vituperates his boss for unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不公平的待遇而痛骂他的老板。
words.en: To criticize or blame someone harshly and angrily.

words.ex: The clan lived in a small village for centuries.
words.ex_cn: 这个氏族几个世纪以来一直住在一个小村庄里。
words.en: A clan is a group of families or relatives who are connected by blood or marriage and who often share the same surname.

words.tr: adj. 爱发号施令的；多管闲事的
words.ex: The officious clerk refused to help unless I filled out another form.
words.ex_cn: 那位爱多管闲事的职员拒绝帮忙，除非我再填一份表格。
words.en: If you describe someone as officious, you are critical of them because they are eager to tell people what to do when you think they should not.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.tr:
v. 调情；轻率地对待
n. 与多人调情的人
words.ex: He flirts with her at the coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在咖啡店向她调情。
words.en: If you flirt with someone, you behave as if you are sexually attracted to them, in a playful or not very serious way.

words.tr: adj. 声音甜美的；悦耳动听的
words.ex: Her mellifluous voice made everyone calm.
words.ex_cn: 她悦耳的声音让每个人都平静下来。
words.en: A mellifluous sound or voice is smooth and pleasant to listen to.

words.tr: adj. 不修边幅的；邋遢的
words.ex: He wore slovenly clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着邋遢的衣服去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as slovenly, you disapprove of them because they are careless and untidy in their appearance or habits.

words.tr: v. 撕碎；劈开；揪扯；割裂
words.ex: The storm rends the tree from its roots.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨将树从根部撕裂。
words.en: To tear or split something apart with great force.

words.ex: He tries to aggrandize himself by lying about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他通过吹嘘自己的成就来抬高自己。
words.en: To increase the power, status, or wealth of someone or something.

words.ex: The two kids stayed in equilibrium on the seesaw.
words.ex_cn: 两个孩子在跷跷板上保持了平衡。
words.en: A state in which opposing forces or influences are balanced.

words.ex: He gave her a scowl when she was late.
words.ex_cn: 她迟到时，他皱了皱眉。
words.en: When someone scowls, they look at someone or something with an angry or irritated expression.

words.tr:
adj. 不可挽救的；屡教不改的；不可救药的
n. 无可救药的人
words.ex: He is an incorrigible liar.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个无可救药的骗子。
words.en: If you describe someone as incorrigible, you mean that they have faults which they seem unable or unwilling to correct, even though they are aware of them.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.ex: He tries to denigrate his rival's ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低对手的想法。
words.en: If you denigrate someone or something, you criticize them unfairly or insult them.

words.ex: The fetid smell came from the old trash.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自旧垃圾。
words.en: Having an extremely unpleasant smell.

words.ex: The wizard conjure a fireball with ancient words.
words.ex_cn: 巫师用古老的咒语召唤出一个火球。
words.en: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

words.tr:
adj. 偏袒的；党派性的
n. 强烈支持者；党羽；游击队员
words.ex: He gave a partisan answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了偏袒的回答。
words.en: A partisan is a strong supporter of a party, cause, or person. It can also refer to a member of an armed group formed to fight secretly against an occupying force.

words.tr: vi. 钙化；变成石灰质; vt. 使钙化；使思想僵化
words.ex: Over time, soft tissues can calcify and become hard.
words.ex_cn: 随着时间的推移，软组织可能会钙化并变硬。
words.en: To calcify means to become or make something hard or inflexible, especially by the deposit of calcium salts.

words.tr: v. 重组；重新设立；使（脱水食物等）恢复原状
words.ex: The committee was reconstituted to address the new challenges.
words.ex_cn: 委员会被重组以应对新的挑战。
words.en: To reconstitute something means to change it back to its original form or to a different form by adding water or another liquid.

words.tr:
adj. 柔软的；可塑的；易弯曲的；有弹性的
v. 使柔软；把（火炮）系在前车上；做热身运动
n. （拖炮车的）前车
words.ex: The gymnast's body is remarkably limber.
words.ex_cn: 这位体操运动员的身体非常柔软。
words.en: Capable of moving or bending easily; flexible.

words.ex: The sudden jolt woke me up.
words.ex_cn: 突然的震动把我惊醒了。
words.en: If something jolts or if something jolts it, it moves suddenly and quite violently.

words.ex: The vendor sells fresh fruits at the market.
words.ex_cn: 这个商贩在市场卖新鲜水果。
words.en: A vendor is a person or company that sells goods or services.

words.ex: Lizards can regenerate their tails.
words.ex_cn: 蜥蜴可以再生尾巴。
words.en: To regenerate means to grow or form again, especially after being damaged or lost, or to improve a place or system by making it more active or successful.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.ex: He abased himself before the king.
words.ex_cn: 他在国王面前贬低自己。
words.en: To abase someone or something means to lower them in rank, status, or esteem.

words.ex: His talent overshadowed his brother's achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华使他兄弟的成就黯然失色。
words.en: If an unpleasant event or feeling overshadows something, it makes it less happy or enjoyable.

words.tr:
v. 轻咬；啃；一点点地吃
n. 一小口；轻咬；少量
words.ex: The dog nibble the biscuit slowly.
words.ex_cn: 狗慢慢地轻咬着饼干。
words.en: To nibble means to take small bites of something, especially food.

words.tr: adj. 絮聒的；饶舌的；多嘴的
words.ex: He is garrulous and talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他话很多，说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as garrulous, you mean that they talk a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.tr: adj. 心烦意乱的；忧心如焚的
words.ex: She was distraught when she lost her dog.
words.ex_cn: 当她丢失了她的狗时，她非常悲痛。
words.en: If someone is distraught, they are so upset and worried that they cannot think clearly.

words.tr:
n. 问题；重要议题；发行（物）；
v. 发行；
words.ex: The main issue is lack of money.
words.ex_cn: 主要问题是缺乏资金。
words.en: An issue is an important subject or problem that people are talking about or arguing about.

words.ex: The slow internet frustrates me.
words.ex_cn: 慢速的网络让我感到沮丧。
words.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to deal with the problems it creates.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.tr:
n. (从事某项活动的)规定期限
v. 吝惜；节省
words.ex: He did a short stint as a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他短暂地当过一段时间老师。
words.en: A stint is a fixed period of time during which someone does a particular job or activity.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.

words.ex: He has a knack for fixing bikes.
words.ex_cn: 他有修自行车的技巧。
words.en: A knack is a special skill or ability that someone has, especially one that is hard to explain or teach.

words.tr: n. 废弃物（树枝、碎石等）；
words.ex: The workers cleared the brash from the construction site.
words.ex_cn: 工人们清除了建筑工地上的废弃物。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as brash, you disapprove of them because you think that they are too confident and aggressive.

words.tr:
n. 滑稽模仿；讽刺作品
adj. 滑稽模仿的；讽刺性作品的
v. 模仿嘲弄
words.ex: The burlesque show was a hit with the audience.
words.ex_cn: 滑稽讽刺表演受到了观众的热烈欢迎。
words.en: A burlesque is a performance or a piece of writing that makes fun of something or someone by copying them in an exaggerated way.

words.ex: The workers load stones from the quarry.
words.ex_cn: 工人们从采石场装载石头。
words.en: A quarry is a place where stone, sand, etc., is dug out of the ground. It can also refer to an animal or person that is being hunted or chased.

words.tr: adj. 五花八门的； v. “variegate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The garden has variegated flowers in many colors.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有五花八门的彩色花朵。
words.en: Having patches, stripes, or marks of different colors; diversified in appearance.

words.tr:
n. 讽刺作品
v. 讽刺
words.ex: The cartoon lampooned the president with funny drawings.
words.ex_cn: 这幅漫画用搞笑的图画讽刺了总统。
words.en: To lampoon someone or something means to criticize them very strongly in a humorous way, especially in a piece of writing.

words.tr:
adj. 即时的；未经准备的；唐突无礼的
adv. 即时地；未经思索地；随便地
words.ex: He gave an offhand answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个即时的回答。
words.en: If you say something offhand, you say it without checking the details or facts of it beforehand.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.ex: He imbibes coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: To imbibe means to drink, especially alcohol, or to absorb or take in something, such as knowledge or ideas.

words.tr:
v. 轻快地掠过；突然换位；搬家
n. 掠过；迅速飞过；偷偷搬家
words.ex: The butterfly flits from flower to flower.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶在花朵间飞舞。
words.en: To move quickly and lightly from one place to another.

words.ex: He got a penalty for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规则而受到惩罚。
words.en: A penalty is a punishment that is imposed on someone for doing something that is against the rules or the law.

words.tr:
n. 抒情诗；歌词
adj. 抒情的
words.ex: He wrote a lyric about the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一首关于日落的抒情诗。
words.en: Lyric refers to the words of a song, especially a popular song, or to a short poem that expresses personal feelings and thoughts.

words.tr:
v. 回火；适得其反
n. 逆火
words.ex: The engine backfired when he pressed the gas pedal.
words.ex_cn: 当他踩下油门时，发动机回火了。
words.en: If a plan or project backfires, it has the opposite result to the one that was intended.

words.tr: adj. 自我中心的；自私自利的
words.ex: He is egoistic and only thinks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他很自私，只考虑自己。
words.en: Egoistic refers to someone who is excessively self-centered or self-interested.

words.ex: The team canvass voters for their opinions.
words.ex_cn: 团队征询选民的意见。
words.en: To canvass means to ask people for their votes or opinions, especially in a political context, or to examine something carefully.

words.ex: He disavow any connection to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 他否认与这起犯罪有任何关联。
words.en: If you disavow something, you say that you are not responsible for it or you do not agree with it.

words.ex: His lateness discommoded everyone else's schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他的迟到给其他人的日程安排带来了不便。
words.en: If someone or something discommodes you, they cause you inconvenience or trouble.

words.tr: v. 舍不得给；节省；克扣
words.ex: She skimped on the ingredients to save money.
words.ex_cn: 她为了省钱，在食材上克扣。
words.en: To skimp means to spend less time, money, or effort on something than is really needed, often resulting in a lower quality outcome.

words.ex: The old man lives in a small hovel.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人住在一间小破屋里。
words.en: A hovel is a small, dirty, and often poorly built house or shelter.

words.tr: adj. 可饮用的；适于饮用的
words.ex: The water is potable.
words.ex_cn: 这水可以饮用。
words.en: Potable water is safe to drink.

words.ex: The cold water gave her a sudden sensation.
words.ex_cn: 冷水给了她一种突然的感觉。
words.en: A sensation is a physical feeling or a reaction of interest or excitement that something causes in a person or in a group of people.

words.ex: The weather can dictate what we wear each day.
words.ex_cn: 天气可以支配我们每天穿什么。
words.en: To dictate means to say or read something aloud for someone else to write down, or to give orders in an authoritative manner.

words.tr:
n. 附属物；
adj. 附属的；
words.ex: The printer is an adjunct to the computer.
words.ex_cn: 打印机是电脑的附属物。
words.en: Something that is added or attached to something else but is not essential to it.

words.tr:
n. 尖塔；尖顶；尖峰；尖岩石；顶点；顶峰
v. 造小尖塔；把...放在极高处
words.ex: The pinnacle of the church reached high into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的尖塔高耸入云。
words.en: The pinnacle of something is the highest point or level that it can reach, especially when it is very good.

words.ex: He acquiesced to his boss's decision.
words.ex_cn: 他默许了老板的决定。
words.en: If you acquiesce in something, you agree to do what someone wants or to accept what they do even though you may not agree with it.

words.ex: He used a match to ignite the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: If you ignite something or if it ignites, it starts burning or explodes.

words.ex: The hen incubate eggs until they hatch.
words.ex_cn: 母鸡孵化鸡蛋直到小鸡孵出。
words.en: to keep eggs warm so that they develop and hatch, or to keep cells, bacteria, etc. at a suitable temperature so that they develop

words.ex: He was a pioneer in space exploration.
words.ex_cn: 他是太空探索的先驱者。
words.en: A pioneer is someone who is one of the first people to do something that others will later develop or continue. Pioneers are also people who are among the first to go to live in a new area, especially in the past when people were trying to settle in new lands.

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；失意的；留恋的
words.ex: She gave a wistful glance at the old photo.
words.ex_cn: 她对着那张旧照片投以怀念的一瞥。
words.en: If you are wistful, you are thinking about something that you want but cannot have, especially something that you used to have in the past.

words.ex: He tries to mediate between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在两个朋友之间调解。
words.en: To intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: He is conversant with basic math.
words.ex_cn: 他熟悉基础数学。
words.en: If you are conversant with something, you are familiar with it and able to deal with it.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.tr: v. 焚化；焚毁；把…烧成灰烬
words.ex: The city will incinerate the trash tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市明天将焚烧垃圾。
words.en: To incinerate something means to burn it until it is reduced to ash.

words.ex: The bakery made a new batch of bread this morning.
words.ex_cn: 这家面包店今天早上做了一批新面包。
words.en: A batch is a quantity or consignment of goods produced at one time.

words.tr: n. 混杂物；集锦；集成曲
words.ex: The band played a medley of old songs.
words.ex_cn: 乐队演奏了一串老歌的混合曲。
words.en: A medley is a mixture of things, especially a mixture of tunes or songs played one after the other.

words.ex: She applied a soothing balm to the wound.
words.ex_cn: 她在伤口上涂了镇痛软膏。
words.en: A balm is a preparation that soothes, heals, or comforts, often applied to the skin.

words.ex: His heterodox ideas shocked the traditional scholars.
words.ex_cn: 他的非正统观点让传统学者感到震惊。
words.en: Heterodox ideas, opinions, or practices are different from the accepted or official ones.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.ex: The teacher commends her for working hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师表扬她学习努力。
words.en: If you commend someone or something, you praise them formally.

words.ex: He is a true patriot who loves his country.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位真正热爱祖国的爱国者。
words.en: A patriot is someone who loves their country and is willing to defend it against enemies or detractors.

words.ex: The table is made of sturdy wood.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是用坚固的木头做的。
words.en: Someone or something that is sturdy looks strong and is unlikely to be easily injured or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 酸的； 苦涩的；尖刻的
words.ex: The lemon juice had an acerbic taste.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬汁有酸味。
words.en: If you say something acerbic, or harshly bitter, you are being sharply critical or sarcastic.

words.ex: He remained imperturbable even when the storm hit.
words.ex_cn: 即使风暴来袭，他依然镇定自若。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperturbable, you mean that they remain calm, even in disturbing or dangerous situations.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；乖戾的；傲慢的
words.ex: The surly man refused to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 那个脾气暴躁的人拒绝打招呼。
words.en: If someone is surly, they are unfriendly and bad-tempered.

words.ex: He gave an oration at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了演讲。
words.en: A formal speech, especially one given on a ceremonial occasion.

words.tr:
v. 预言；预测
n. （古罗马）占兆官；占卜师
words.ex: The early reviews augur well for the success of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 早期的评论预示着这部电影将取得成功。
words.en: to predict or foretell, especially from signs or omens

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.tr: adj. 一定会；密切相关的；有义务的； v. “bind”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is bound to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他一定会赢得比赛。
words.en: If one person, thing, or situation is bound to another, they are closely connected with each other, and it is difficult for them to be separated or to escape from each other. If you say that something is bound to happen, you mean that you are sure it will happen, because it is a natural consequence of something that is already known or exists.

words.ex: He showed disdain for the lazy students.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些懒惰的学生表现出蔑视。
words.en: If you feel disdain for someone or something, you dislike them because you think that they are inferior or unimportant.

words.tr: adv. 不管愿不愿意地；乱七八糟地；无计划地; adj. 不管愿不愿意的；乱七八糟的
words.ex: The project was completed willy-nilly, with no clear plan.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目无计划地完成了，没有明确的计划。
words.en: If something happens willy-nilly, it happens whether people want it to or not, often in a way that is not organized or planned.

words.tr: n. 长篇抨击激烈演说
words.ex: He went on a tirade about slow internet.
words.ex_cn: 他大发雷霆，抱怨网速太慢。
words.en: A tirade is a long, angry speech of criticism or accusation.

words.ex: He blurted out the secret by accident.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心说出了秘密。
words.en: If someone blurts something, they say it suddenly, after trying hard to keep quiet or to keep it secret.

words.tr: adj. 不寻常的；非传统的；不落俗套的
words.ex: He likes offbeat movies that no one else understands.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢那些别人都不理解的古怪电影。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as offbeat, you mean that they are different from what is usual or expected in an unusual and appealing way.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；软弱的；无活力的
words.ex: The leaves looked flaccid after the long dry spell.
words.ex_cn: 长时间干旱后，树叶看起来软弱无力。
words.en: Lacking firmness, resilience, or muscle tone; soft and limp.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.tr: v. 使负罪；指控…有罪；牵连
words.ex: He did not want to incriminate his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让他的朋友涉罪。
words.en: If something incriminates someone, it suggests that they are guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.

words.ex: We arrived at the opportune moment, just as the meeting was starting.
words.ex_cn: 我们到达得很及时，正好会议刚开始。
words.en: If something happens at an opportune time or is opportune, it happens at the time that is most convenient for someone or most likely to lead to success.

words.ex: The incandescent bulb gives off a warm light.
words.ex_cn: 白炽灯发出温暖的光。
words.en: Emitting light as a result of being heated.

words.ex: He needs time to recuperate after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他需要时间在手术后恢复。
words.en: To recuperate means to recover from illness or exertion, or to regain or make up for something lost or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 摇摇欲坠的；破烂不堪的
words.ex: The old house was ramshackle and needed repair.
words.ex_cn: 那栋老房子摇摇欲坠，需要修理。
words.en: A ramshackle building or vehicle is in very bad condition and in danger of falling down.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.tr:
v. 狼吞虎咽；吞并；火鸡咯咯叫
n. 火鸡叫声
words.ex: The dog will gobble up its food quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗会很快把食物狼吞虎咽地吃掉。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, often making a noise.

words.ex: She is a comely girl with a sweet smile.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个面容姣好、带着甜美微笑的姑娘。
words.en: Pleasant to look at; attractive.

words.ex: The spoon has a concave surface.
words.ex_cn: 勺子有一个凹的表面。
words.en: A concave surface is curved inward, like the inside of a bowl.

words.tr:
v. 口吃；结结巴巴地说
n. 口吃；结巴
words.ex: He stammers when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 他紧张时会结巴。
words.en: If someone stammers, they speak with difficulty, hesitating and repeating words or sounds.

words.tr: n. 反复无常；任性；怪想
words.ex: Her decision to quit the job was a sudden caprice.
words.ex_cn: 她决定辞职是突如其来的任性之举。
words.en: A sudden and unaccountable change of mood or behavior.

words.ex: The dog grovelled on the ground to beg for food.
words.ex_cn: 狗趴在地上乞求食物。
words.en: If you grovel, you behave in a very submissive way in order to show that you are sorry for something wrong that you have done or to try to get someone to forgive you or do something for you.

words.tr: adj. 迟缓的；呆钝的；不活泼的；蛰伏的
words.ex: The cat was torpid in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 猫在阳光下懒洋洋的。
words.en: If you are torpid, you are mentally or physically inactive, especially because you are feeling lazy or sleepy.

words.ex: The army stopped the incursion at the border.
words.ex_cn: 军队在边境阻止了入侵。
words.en: An incursion is a sudden attack on or invasion of a place.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.tr:
n. 振动；剧跳；极度的紧张不安；抽搐；痉挛；“jitter”的复数
v. 颤抖；战战兢兢；紧张不安；紧张地说；使…惶恐不安；“jitter”的第三人称单数
words.ex: The old bridge began to show jitters when the truck passed over it.
words.ex_cn: 当卡车驶过时，这座旧桥开始出现振动。
words.en: A feeling of extreme nervousness.

words.tr:
adj. 迷人的；令人沉醉的
v. 施魔法于；蛊惑；“bewitch”的现在分词
words.ex: She had a bewitching smile that could light up any room.
words.ex_cn: 她有一个迷人的微笑，能让任何房间都亮起来。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bewitching, you mean they are so attractive or interesting that they seem to have a magical effect on you.

words.tr: adj. 抱怨的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: She had a querulous tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种爱发牢骚的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as querulous, you mean that they complain about things in a rather bad-tempered way.

words.ex: He tried to inculpate his friend for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把错误归咎于他的朋友。
words.en: To inculpate someone means to accuse them of a crime or to make them seem guilty of it.

words.tr:
n. 救援；援助者
v. 救援
words.ex: The nurse gave succor to the injured man.
words.ex_cn: 护士向受伤的男人提供了援助。
words.en: Succor is assistance and support given to someone in times of hardship or distress.

words.ex: His story was credible and easy to believe.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事可信且容易让人相信。
words.en: If something or someone is credible, they can be believed or trusted.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.ex: The company will withhold his salary until he signs the contract.
words.ex_cn: 公司会扣留他的工资，直到他签署合同。
words.en: If you withhold something that someone wants, you refuse to let them have it.

words.ex: The wound began to fester if not cleaned.
words.ex_cn: 如果不清洗，伤口就会恶化。
words.en: If a wound festers, it becomes infected, making it worse.

words.ex: The abstruse math problem confused the students.
words.ex_cn: 这个深奥的数学问题让学生们感到困惑。
words.en: Difficult to understand; obscure.

words.tr:
n. 勒索；敲诈
v. 勒索；讹诈
words.ex: He threatened to tell the truth unless she paid him money — that's blackmail.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁说，除非她付钱，否则就说出真相——这就是敲诈。
words.en: Blackmail is the action of threatening to reveal a secret about someone, unless they do something you want, such as give you money.

words.ex: His sepulchral voice made everyone feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 他那阴森的声音让每个人都感到悲伤。
words.en: If you describe something as sepulchral, you mean that it is rather solemn and depressing.

words.tr: v. 含糊其辞；说模棱两可的话
words.ex: He equivocates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他含糊其辞。
words.en: If you equivocate, you use ambiguous language in order to deceive people or to avoid speaking directly about something.

words.ex: The injury led to a sequela of chronic pain.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤导致了慢性疼痛的后遗症。
words.en: A condition which is the consequence of a previous disease or injury.

words.ex: The farmer milks the cow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上给母牛挤奶。
words.en: A cow is a large female animal that is kept on farms for its milk.

words.ex: The magazine has a glossy cover.
words.ex_cn: 这本杂志有一个光滑的封面。
words.en: Something that is glossy is smooth and shiny.

words.ex: The issue polarized the community into two opposing groups.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题使社区分裂成了两个对立的群体。
words.en: To polarize means to cause something, especially a group or an issue, to divide into two sharply contrasting groups or sets of opinions or beliefs.

words.ex: The hot weather enervates him.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让他感到乏力。
words.en: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.

words.tr:
v. 击退；回绝；憎恶
n. 拒斥；击退；严拒
words.ex: The soldiers repulse the enemy attack.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们击退了敌人的进攻。
words.en: If you repulse someone, you reject them or make them feel disgusted.

words.ex: He was reluctant to leave his home.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意离开家。
words.en: If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: The dullard never understood the math lesson.
words.ex_cn: 这个愚笨的人从未理解过数学课。
words.en: A dullard is someone who is considered to be rather slow and not very intelligent.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.ex: She had a puckish grin on her face when she hid his keys.
words.ex_cn: 她藏起他的钥匙时，脸上露出了淘气的笑容。
words.en: If you describe someone as puckish, you mean that they playfully cause trouble or behave in a mischievous way.

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.tr: n. 抱偏见的人；执拗的人；顽固者
words.ex: He is a bigot who hates people different from him.
words.ex_cn: 他是个偏执的人，讨厌与他不同的人。
