words.en: Worldly means relating to the world and the practical matters of life, rather than to spiritual or religious matters.

words.tr:
v. 装作教皇似地说话；自以为是地谈论；目空一切地议论
n. 教皇职务（或在任时期）
words.ex: He loves to pontificate about politics.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢目空一切地谈论政治。
words.en: To pontificate means to speak or behave in a pompous or dogmatic way, often giving opinions as if they were facts.

words.ex: There are only two extant copies of the ancient book.
words.ex_cn: 这本古书现存只有两份。
words.en: If something is extant, it is still in existence, in spite of being very old.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；衷心的；诚挚的；
words.ex: He is a devout Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名虔诚的基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: If you describe someone as devout, you mean that they have a deep religious faith.

words.ex: His reputation was besmirched by the false accusations.
words.ex_cn: 他的名声被这些虚假的指控玷污了。
words.en: To besmirch someone or something means to spoil their good reputation.

words.tr:
n. 路障；栅栏；阻碍
v. 设路障；阻挡
words.ex: The police put up a barricade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察设了一个路障来阻止人群。
words.en: A barricade is a temporary structure that is built across a road, entrance, or other route to prevent people from passing. It can also refer to the act of creating such a structure.

words.tr: adj. 兴致很高的；很有滋味的
words.ex: The party had a zesty atmosphere with lively music and dancing.
words.ex_cn: 派对气氛非常活跃，有充满活力的音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Having a strong, pleasant, and somewhat spicy flavor or smell; lively and pleasing.

words.ex: His rectitude in business dealings was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业交易中的正直是众所周知的。
words.en: Moral integrity; honesty and correctness of judgement or behaviour.

words.tr: adj. 矫揉造作的；不自然的；守规矩的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: Her mannered speech was hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 她矫揉造作的言辞让人难以理解。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or a work of art as mannered, you dislike it because it is elaborate or formal, and therefore seems false or artificial.

words.tr: v. 豪饮；痛饮；开怀畅饮
words.ex: He quaffed the cold drink quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速地喝下了那杯冷饮。
words.en: To drink (a beverage) heartily and with gusto.

words.ex: Their argument was acrimonious and lasted all night.
words.ex_cn: 他们的争论很尖刻，持续了一整晚。
words.en: If you say that an argument or conversation is acrimonious, you mean that it is bitter and angry because the people involved disagree with each other.

words.tr: adj. 游历的；游离不定的；行为不当的；出轨的
words.ex: The errant knight traveled far across the land.
words.ex_cn: 这位游历的骑士穿越了广袤的土地。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as errant, you mean that they have strayed from the proper course or standards.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的；朝生暮死的
words.ex: The flowers are ephemeral and last only one day.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是短暂的，只持续一天。
words.en: Something that is ephemeral lasts for only a very short time.

words.tr: adj. 愚昧的；昏庸的；愚笨的
words.ex: His fatuous smile made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他那愚蠢的微笑让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe a person, action, or remark as fatuous, you mean that they are extremely silly, showing a lack of intelligence or thought.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；激昂地说
n. 喧闹的话；夸口话；叫喊
words.ex: He went on a rant about bad service.
words.ex_cn: 他大肆抱怨服务很差。
words.en: To speak or write in an angry or violent manner, often for a long time.

words.ex: The queen was resplendent in her golden crown.
words.ex_cn: 女王戴着金色王冠，光彩夺目。
words.en: Something that is resplendent is very bright and attractive, often because it is richly decorated or very colorful.

words.tr:
adj. 有生命的；有活力的
v. 使具活力；做成动画
words.ex: The cartoon characters are animate and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 这些卡通角色是有生命的，充满活力。
words.en: To animate something means to give it life or to make it lively and energetic.

words.ex: He cannot comprehend the simple math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他无法理解这个简单的数学问题。
words.en: To comprehend something means to understand it fully.

words.tr: adj. 污秽的；肮脏丑恶的；恶劣的
words.ex: The seamy side of the entertainment industry was exposed in the documentary.
words.ex_cn: 这部纪录片揭露了娱乐行业丑恶的一面。
words.en: If you describe something as seamy, you mean that it involves unpleasant aspects of life such as crime, prostitution, or violence.

words.tr: adj. 平庸陈腐的；过于感伤的
words.ex: The movie's ending was so bathetic that it made everyone cringe.
words.ex_cn: 电影的结局如此陈腐，以至于让每个人都感到不适。
words.en: If you describe something as bathetic, you mean that it is overly sentimental or trying too hard to be serious or dramatic, often resulting in a disappointing or underwhelming effect.

words.tr: adj. 狭窄的； v. “cramp”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The tiny room was cramped and hard to move in.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间很狭窄，很难活动。
words.en: If a place is cramped, it is not big enough for the people or things in it, so that it is difficult to move around or to use things properly.

words.ex: The teacher designated him as the group leader.
words.ex_cn: 老师指派他为组长。
words.en: If you designate someone or something as a particular thing, you formally give them that description or name.

words.ex: The residue left in the cup was sugar.
words.ex_cn: 杯子里留下的残留物是糖。
words.en: A residue of something is a small amount that remains after the main part has gone or been taken or used.

words.tr: n. 壁炉的栅栏；护舷；挡泥板；防卫物
words.ex: The ashes fell behind the fender.
words.ex_cn: 灰烬落在了壁炉的栅栏后面。
words.en: A fender is a barrier or cushion between a vehicle and the outside world, designed to absorb the shock of collision or to protect the vehicle's body from damage.

words.tr:
int. 呸；嘘
n. 嘘声
v. 发出嘘声
words.ex: The crowd gave a loud boo when the player missed the goal.
words.ex_cn: 当球员错失进球时，观众发出了大声的嘘声。
words.en: If you boo a speaker or performer, you shout 'boo' or make other loud sounds to indicate that you do not like them, their opinions, or their performance.

words.ex: He gratifies his parents by getting good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他通过取得好成绩来让父母感到欣慰。
words.en: If you are gratified by something, it gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.tr:
adj. 该得的；应得的
v. 值得；应得；“merit”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His hard work merited the recognition he received.
words.ex_cn: 他的辛勤工作值得他得到的认可。
words.en: Deserved or earned, especially through hard work or good behavior.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: They rejoice when the sun comes out.
words.ex_cn: 当太阳出来时，他们欢呼。
words.en: To feel or show great joy or delight.

words.ex: He flushes the toilet after using it.
words.ex_cn: 他用完厕所后冲水。
words.en: If you flush, your face goes red because you are hot or ill, or because you are feeling a strong emotion such as embarrassment or anger. To flush a toilet means to cause water to pass through it in order to clean it.

words.ex: The kitchen must be sanitary to prevent illness.
words.ex_cn: 厨房必须保持清洁以防止疾病。
words.en: relating to the conditions that affect hygiene and health, especially the supply of sewage facilities and clean drinking water

words.ex: He delves into the history of ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 他探究古代文明的历史。
words.en: If you delve into something, you try to discover new information about it by searching or investigating carefully.

words.tr: adj. 卑鄙的；污秽的；肮脏的
words.ex: He made a sordid deal to cheat his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一笔卑鄙的交易来欺骗他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as sordid, you mean that it is very immoral or dishonest.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.ex: He showed deference to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师表示尊敬。
words.en: Deference is a polite and respectful attitude towards someone, often because they are older or more experienced than you.

words.tr: adj. 羞愧的；卑躬屈膝的
words.ex: He looked hangdog after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他一副垂头丧气的样子。
words.en: If someone has a hangdog expression, they look sad, ashamed, or guilty.

words.tr:
v. 乱摸；摸索；笨手笨脚地做
n. 摸索；笨手笨脚
words.ex: He fumbled for his keys in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中乱摸着找钥匙。
words.en: If you fumble with something, you try to hold, move, or find it with your hands in a clumsy way.

words.ex: He bought a small figurine from the market.
words.ex_cn: 他从市场上买了一个小雕像。
words.en: A figurine is a small ornamental statuette.

words.tr: n. 蒙太奇；画面剪辑；合成画；大杂烩
words.ex: The movie ends with a montage of old photos.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以一组旧照片的蒙太奇结尾。
words.en: A montage is a technique in film editing in which a series of short shots are edited into a sequence to condense space, time, and information.

words.ex: The inexorable flow of time cannot be stopped.
words.ex_cn: 时间不可阻挡地流逝。
words.en: If you describe something as inexorable, you mean that it is impossible to stop or prevent from happening.

words.ex: The book has a gloss at the bottom of each page.
words.ex_cn: 这本书每页底部都有注释。
words.en: A gloss is a bright shine on the surface of something. It can also refer to a superficial appearance or interpretation that conceals the true nature of something.

words.ex: The scientist debunked the myth that sugar makes children hyper.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家揭穿了糖会使孩子多动的谬论。
words.en: If you debunk a widely held belief, you show that it is false. If you debunk something that is widely admired, you show that it is not as good as people think it is.

words.tr:
v. 挥；舞动；炫耀地显示
n. 挥舞
words.ex: He brandished a knife to scare the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他挥舞着一把刀吓唬小偷。
words.en: If you brandish something, especially a weapon, you wave it about in a threatening way.

words.tr: adj. 整洁时髦的；设计精妙的
words.ex: He wears a natty suit to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天穿一件时髦的西装去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as natty, you mean that their clothes are smart and fashionable.

words.ex: The volcano began to disgorge lava.
words.ex_cn: 火山开始喷出岩浆。
words.en: If something disgorges its contents or if it is disgorged, its contents come out, often in a sudden and violent way.

words.tr:
adj. 醉人的
n. 酒精饮料；致醉药物
words.ex: Alcohol is a common intoxicant.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是一种常见的致醉物。
words.en: An intoxicant is a substance that can cause intoxication, such as alcohol or drugs.

words.tr:
v. 抱怨；发牢骚；绞痛
n. 抱怨；肠绞痛
words.ex: He always gripes about the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他总是抱怨天气。
words.en: If you gripe, you complain about something in a persistent, irritating way.

words.tr: adj. 衣冠楚楚的；干净利落的；短小精悍的
words.ex: He was a dapper man, always impeccably dressed.
words.ex_cn: 他是个衣冠楚楚的人，总是穿着无可挑剔。
words.en: If you describe a man as dapper, you mean that he is small and neat in appearance and moves quickly and energetically.

words.ex: Despite the rehabilitation program, he continued to recidivate.
words.ex_cn: 尽管参加了康复计划，他还是继续再犯。
words.en: To return to a previous pattern of behavior, especially criminal behavior, after having stopped it for a period of time.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；公然的；喧闹的
words.ex: He made a blatant lie to avoid punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他为了逃避惩罚，公然撒了谎。
words.en: If you describe an action as blatant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way, often with a lack of shame or embarrassment.

words.ex: He felt trepidation before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到恐惧。
words.en: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

words.tr: adj. 同时发生的；同步的；
words.ex: The two events happened synchronous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.ex: He peruses the newspaper every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上浏览报纸。
words.en: To read or examine something carefully or thoroughly.

words.ex: The indigent man asked for food at the shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这位贫困的人在收容所里请求食物。
words.en: Someone who is indigent is very poor.

words.tr: n. 冒名顶替者；冒名行骗者
words.ex: He was exposed as an impostor who had been posing as a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他被揭露为一个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: An impostor is someone who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive people.

words.ex: The children played in the grit near the road.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在路边的沙砾中玩耍。
words.en: Grit is very small pieces of stone. It is often used to make surfaces less slippery. Grit is also a quality of character that enables someone to continue with determination in the face of difficulties.

words.tr: adj. 愚笨的；癫狂的；痴傻的
words.ex: He wore a daft hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶傻气的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as daft, you mean that they are silly, foolish, or crazy.

words.ex: He noticed the nuance in her voice.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了她声音中的细微差别。
words.en: A very slight difference in meaning, sound, color, or someone's feelings that is not usually very obvious.

words.tr: v. 晒太阳（取暖）；沉浸于
words.ex: He basks in the warm sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 他沐浴在温暖的阳光下。
words.en: If you bask in the sunshine, you lie somewhere sunny and enjoy the heat.

words.ex: His ken does not include quantum physics.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识范围不包括量子物理。
words.en: Ken is the range of one's knowledge or understanding.

words.ex: The company preempted its rivals by launching the product early.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司通过提前推出产品抢先行动。
words.en: To preempt something means to do or say something before someone else does, especially to prevent them from doing or saying it.

words.tr:
adj. 无准备的；即兴的；即席的
adv. 无准备地；即兴地；即席地
words.ex: He gave an impromptu speech at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上做了一次即兴演讲。
words.en: An impromptu action is one that you do without planning or organizing it in advance.

words.ex: The teacher berated the student for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而责备了他。
words.en: To scold or criticize someone angrily.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.tr: n. 窥淫癖者；好刺探他人隐私者
words.ex: He was arrested for being a voyeur, spying on people in their private moments.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窥他人隐私时刻而被捕，是一个窥淫狂者。
words.en: A voyeur is someone who gets sexual pleasure from secretly watching other people, especially when they are naked or having sex.

words.tr: n. 打字（或排印）文稿的小错误
words.ex: He found a typo in his email.
words.ex_cn: 他在邮件里发现了一个拼写错误。
words.en: A typo is a mistake in the way something is printed or written.

words.tr: adj. 惊人的；巨大的；奇异的；巨大的；
words.ex: He showed a prodigious memory for names.
words.ex_cn: 他对名字有着惊人的记忆力。
words.en: If you describe something as prodigious, you are emphasizing that it is very large or impressive.

words.tr: adj. 清醒的；严肃的；素淡的；
words.ex: He stayed sober after drinking only water.
words.ex_cn: 他只喝了水，保持清醒。
words.en: If you are sober, you are not drunk. If you are sober, you are serious and thoughtful.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: He faced obloquy for speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因说出真相而遭受非议。
words.en: Obloquy is strong public criticism or verbal abuse.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；勤苦工作的
words.ex: He is sedulous in practicing piano every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天勤奋地练习钢琴。
words.en: If you describe someone as sedulous, you mean that they work hard and pay great attention to detail.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: The police used surveillance to watch the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用监视来观察那栋大楼。
words.en: The careful watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army, because of a crime that has happened or is expected.

words.tr: adj. 讲究礼仪的；隆重的
words.ex: He gave a ceremonious speech at the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他在婚礼上发表了一篇庄重的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as ceremonious, you mean that they are very formal or polite.

words.tr:
v. 嘲讽；嘲弄；相匹配
n. 嘲弄；挖苦
words.ex: His story doesn't jibe with the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事与事实不符。
words.en: If one thing jibes with another, they agree or are very similar.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.ex: He has great stamina for running long distances.
words.ex_cn: 他有很强的耐力来跑长距离。
words.en: Stamina is the physical or mental energy needed to do a tiring activity for a long time.

words.tr:
adj. 珍爱的；珍视的
v. 珍爱；爱惜；怀念；怀有（感情）；抱有（希望）；“cherish”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She kept her cherished doll from childhood.
words.ex_cn: 她保留了从小珍爱的洋娃娃。
words.en: If you cherish something, you regard it as important and valuable, and you try to keep it or protect it.

words.tr: v. 计算；“calculate”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 计算的；
words.ex: He calculated the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速计算了总费用。
words.en: If something is calculated to have a particular effect, it is deliberately done in order to have that effect.

words.ex: The government will promulgate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将公布新规则。
words.en: To promulgate means to make a new law or rule known officially and publicly.

words.tr: adj. 病态的；心理不健康的
words.ex: He has a morbid fear of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗有一种病态的恐惧。
words.en: If you describe a person or their interest in something as morbid, you mean that they are very interested in unpleasant things, especially death, and you think this is strange.

words.ex: The wooden beams are bracing the wall.
words.ex_cn: 木梁正在支撑着墙壁。
words.en: Invigorating or stimulating, especially in a way that strengthens or refreshes.

words.tr: n. 宗派主义；教派主义
words.ex: The conflict grew because of sectarianism.
words.ex_cn: 由于宗派主义，冲突加剧了。
words.en: Sectarianism is strong support for the religious or political group that you belong to, often combined with a dislike or hatred of other groups.

words.ex: The chair is inanimate.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是没有生命的。
words.en: Something that is inanimate is not alive, such as a rock or a chair. It can also describe something that lacks energy or spirit.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.tr:
n. 双关语
v. 说双关语
words.ex: He made a bad pun and everyone groaned.
words.ex_cn: 他开了个蹩脚的玩笑，大家都皱起了眉头。
words.en: A pun is a clever and amusing use of a word or phrase with two meanings, or of words with the same sound but different meanings.

words.ex: He made an impious joke about the sacred temple.
words.ex_cn: 他对神圣的寺庙开了一个不敬的玩笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as impious, you mean that they show a lack of respect for religious practices or beliefs.

words.ex: The spy tried to infiltrate the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 间谍试图渗透敌方基地。
words.en: To enter or gain access to (an organization, place, etc.) surreptitiously and gradually, especially in order to acquire secret information.

words.tr: adj. 下意识的；潜意识的；
words.ex: The ad used subliminal messages to influence buyers.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告使用了下意识的信息来影响买家。
words.en: Subliminal refers to something that is below the threshold of sensation or consciousness; it is perceived by or affecting someone's mind without their being aware of it.

words.tr: adj. 颖悟的；敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perspicacious and notices small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 她很敏锐，能注意到细小的错误。
words.en: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things.

words.tr: adj. 抛光的；磨光的；擦亮的； v. 擦亮；磨光；“polish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The polished table reflected the light.
words.ex_cn: 抛光的桌子反射着光线。
words.en: If something is polished, it has been made smooth and shiny by rubbing it with a cloth or a special substance.

words.ex: He kneads dough every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上揉面团。
words.en: To knead is to press and stretch dough or another substance with your hands in order to make it smooth and ready to use.

words.ex: The ferocious wind knocked down the tree.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的风把树吹倒了。
words.en: A ferocious animal or person is very fierce and violent.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；清晰的
words.ex: The lake water is limpid and clear.
words.ex_cn: 湖水清澈透明。
words.en: Clear and transparent, especially in a way that makes it easy to understand.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.ex: He enjoyed the adventure through vicarious experiences in books.
words.ex_cn: 他通过书中的间接体验享受了冒险。
words.en: Experienced or felt by watching, hearing about, or reading about someone else rather than by doing something yourself.

words.ex: The table has a wooden veneer on top.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子的表面有一层木制饰板。
words.en: A veneer is a thin layer of wood or other material that is used to cover a surface, especially in furniture making, to make it look more attractive.

words.ex: The brewery uses fresh mash to make beer.
words.ex_cn: 酿酒厂使用新鲜的麦芽浆来酿造啤酒。
words.en: To crush or smash something into a soft, pulpy mass.

words.ex: The high fine will deter people from breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款会制止人们违法。
words.en: If something deters you from doing something, it makes you not want to do it or continue doing it.

words.ex: He espouses simple ideas about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他拥护关于正义的简单理念。
words.en: If you espouse a particular policy, cause, or belief, you become very interested in it and give your support to it.

words.ex: He converts old paper into new notebooks.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧纸张转换成新笔记本。
words.en: To change something into a different form or to change someone's beliefs, especially their religious beliefs.

words.tr: v. 使士气低落；使失去斗志
words.ex: The bad news demoralized the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队士气低落。
words.en: If something demoralizes someone, it makes them lose so much confidence in what they are doing that they want to give up.

words.ex: He is fussy about his food.
words.ex_cn: 他对食物很挑剔。
words.en: Someone who is fussy is very concerned with unimportant details and is difficult to please.

words.ex: He is diffident when he speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时很腼腆。
words.en: If you are diffident, you are rather shy and do not enjoy talking about yourself or being noticed by other people.

words.tr:
v. 说傻话；胡说；淌口水；流鼻涕
n. 胡言乱语；糊涂话
words.ex: He was so tired that he started to drivel incoherently.
words.ex_cn: 他太累了，开始胡言乱语。
words.en: If you describe what someone says as drivel, you mean that it is nonsense.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.tr: n. 施教者；好为人师的人；卖弄学问者
words.ex: The pedagogue taught children to read and write.
words.ex_cn: 这位教师教孩子们读书写字。
words.en: A pedagogue is a teacher, especially one who is strict or old-fashioned in their methods.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.ex: The volcano is quiescent now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive.

words.ex: The king will instate a new prime minister next week.
words.ex_cn: 国王下周将任命一位新的首相。
words.en: To instate someone in a position or job means to formally establish them in that position or job.

words.tr: adj. 偶然的；外来的；不定的
words.ex: The plant grew adventitious roots from its stem.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物从茎上长出了不定根。
words.en: Adventitious means happening or carried on according to chance rather than design or inherent nature.

words.ex: The teacher gave an encomium to the student for her perfect score.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生得了满分而给予了赞美。
words.en: A formal expression of praise; a eulogy.

words.tr:
n. 滞后；延迟；
v. 落后；缓慢移动；
words.ex: There is a lag between the signal and the response.
words.ex_cn: 信号和响应之间有滞后。
words.en: If one thing or person lags behind another thing or person, their progress is slower than that of the other.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.tr: adj. 兴奋期待的；急切期待的
words.ex: The children were agog at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们对魔术表演感到无比惊奇。
words.en: If you are agog, you are very eager or excited to see or hear something.

words.tr: v. 犯罪；做错事；“commit”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 忠诚的；
words.ex: He was committed for stealing a car.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷车而被定罪。
words.en: If you are committed to something, you are willing to give your time and energy to it because you believe in it.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.ex: The cat creeps slowly toward the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹑手蹑脚地向鸟靠近。
words.en: To move slowly and quietly, especially in a way that does not attract attention.

words.tr: adj. 琐碎的；微不足道的；心胸狭窄的
words.ex: He got angry over a petty mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一个微不足道的错误生气了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as petty, you mean that they care too much about small, unimportant things and perhaps that they are unnecessarily unkind.

words.ex: His views are antithetical to hers.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与她的观点是对偶的。
words.en: Directly opposed or contrasted; mutually incompatible.

words.ex: The colors in the rainbow cover a wide spectrum.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹中的颜色覆盖了广泛的范围。
words.en: A spectrum is a range of a particular type of thing, often a range of colors, ideas, or opinions.

words.ex: The stain on the carpet is a mar.
words.ex_cn: 地毯上的污渍是一个污点。
words.en: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

words.ex: The smile on his face was illusory.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上的微笑是虚假的。
words.en: If something is illusory, it is not real or true, although it may seem to be.

words.ex: He used a clever ruse to escape from the prison.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了一个巧妙的计策从监狱逃脱。
words.en: A ruse is a trick or plan that is used to deceive someone.

words.tr:
v. 含混不清地说话；诋毁；诽谤
n. 诽谤；诋毁；污辱
words.ex: He slurrs his words when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，说话含糊不清。
words.en: If someone slurs their speech or if their speech slurs, they do not pronounce each word clearly, because they are drunk, ill, or sleepy. A slur is an insulting remark which could damage someone's reputation.

words.tr: v. 使窘迫；使困惑；挫败
words.ex: The silly question discomfit the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个愚蠢的问题让老师感到窘迫。
words.en: To make someone feel uneasy or embarrassed.

words.ex: His salary is commensurate with his experience.
words.ex_cn: 他的薪水与他的经验相称。
words.en: If the level of one thing is commensurate with another, the first level is in proportion to the second.

words.ex: My mentor helped me choose my career path.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮助我选择了职业道路。
words.en: A mentor is a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school.

words.tr: v. 使饱足；使厌腻；充分满足
words.ex: The big meal satiated his hunger.
words.ex_cn: 这顿丰盛的饭填饱了他的肚子。
words.en: To satisfy a desire or need fully.

words.tr:
adj. 倾心的；被迷住的
v. 迷住；使迷恋；“enamor”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was enamored with the idea of traveling the world.
words.ex_cn: 他迷恋上了环游世界的想法。
words.en: If you are enamored of something or someone, you are very fond of them or very interested in them.

words.ex: The rupture in the pipe caused a flood.
words.ex_cn: 管道的破裂导致了洪水。
words.en: A rupture is a severe injury in which an internal part of your body tears or bursts open, or the act of breaking or bursting something.

words.tr: adj. 令人震惊的；使大吃一惊的； v. “astound”的现在分词；
words.ex: The magician's trick was astounding.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师的魔术令人震惊。
words.en: If something is astounding, it is so surprising or so impressive that it is difficult to believe.

words.ex: The onerous workload made her tired every day.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量让她每天都很累。
words.en: If you describe a task as onerous, you dislike having to do it because you find it difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 易变的；无常的；感情不专的
words.ex: He is fickle and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他善变，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as fickle, you disapprove of them because they keep changing their mind about what they like or want.

words.ex: He is an addict who cannot stop smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他是个无法戒烟的瘾君子。
words.en: An addict is someone who is unable to stop taking harmful drugs, or someone who is very interested in something and spends a lot of time doing it.

words.ex: The remnant of the old wall still stands.
words.ex_cn: 这堵旧墙的残余部分仍然矗立着。
words.en: A remnant is a small remaining quantity of something.

words.tr: adj. 使人晕眩的；头晕的；轻浮的
words.ex: She felt giddy after spinning around.
words.ex_cn: 她转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel giddy, you feel unsteady and think that you are about to fall over, usually because you are not well or because you are excited or frightened.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The unexpected news discombobulated her.
words.ex_cn: 突如其来的消息使她感到困惑。
words.en: To discombobulate someone means to confuse them a lot.

words.ex: The sun can dehydrate your skin quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳会很快使你的皮肤脱水。
words.en: To dehydrate something means to remove all the water from it, often in order to preserve it. If you dehydrate, you lose too much water from your body, usually because of illness or extreme heat.

words.tr: adj. 灵巧的（手）；熟练的；敏捷的
words.ex: He is dexterous with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手很灵巧。
words.en: Someone who is dexterous is skillful with their hands.

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.tr: adj. 艳丽的；炫耀的；神气活现的
words.ex: He wears flamboyant clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿著華麗的衣服來引人注目。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting.

words.tr:
v. 弄皱；弄乱
n. 皱纹；皱褶
words.ex: He rumpled his shirt before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议前把衬衫弄皱了。
words.en: To make something, especially fabric or paper, less smooth by pressing or handling it roughly.

words.tr:
n. 海峡；渠道；河床；频道；
v. 引导；
words.ex: The English Channel separates England from France.
words.ex_cn: 英吉利海峡将英格兰与法国分隔开。
words.en: A channel is a television station and the programs that it broadcasts. A channel is also a method or system that people use to send information, goods, etc. to each other.

words.tr: adj. 洪亮的；声音极大的
words.ex: His stentorian voice filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 他洪亮的声音充满了整个房间。
words.en: A stentorian voice is very loud and powerful.

words.ex: He has a disinclination to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意在公众场合讲话。
words.en: A disinclination to do something is a feeling of not wanting to do it.

words.ex: He remembers those halcyon days of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他怀念那些童年的宁静时光。
words.en: A halcyon time is a time in the past that was peaceful or happy.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.tr:
n. 曲柄杖；钩；弯曲处；骗子
v. （使）弯曲；使成钩状
words.ex: The old man walked with a wooden crook.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人拿着一根木制曲柄杖走路。
words.en: A crook is a person who is dishonest or a criminal, or it can refer to a bend or curve in something.

words.tr: v. 使人耿耿于怀；令人怀恨
words.ex: The unfair comment still rankles him.
words.ex_cn: 那句不公平的话仍让他耿耿于怀。
words.en: If something rankles, it continues to cause you irritation, bitterness, or pain, often because you think it was unfair.

words.tr:
adj. 同年代的
n. 同时代的人
words.ex: The two ancient temples are coeval.
words.ex_cn: 这两座古代神庙是同时期的。
words.en: Having the same age or date of origin; contemporary.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.ex: He is an equable man who never gets angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个性情恬静的人，从不生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as equable, you mean that they are calm, cheerful, and fair with other people, even in difficult circumstances.

words.tr: v. 使合格；使具有资格；
words.ex: He studied hard to qualify for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以获得这份工作的资格。
words.en: To qualify means to meet the necessary conditions or standards to be eligible for something or to perform a particular role.

words.ex: Birds are migratory in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天是迁徙的。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by migration; tending to migrate.

words.tr:
v. 倒退；退步；退化
n. 倒退；退步；退化
words.ex: The patient regressed to a childlike state after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，病人退回到了孩童般的状态。
words.en: If you regress, you return to a previous and less advanced stage of development.

words.ex: He is a zealot for environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心者。
words.en: A zealot is someone who is extremely enthusiastic about something, especially religion or politics.

words.ex: The smoke from the factory is noxious.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟雾是有害的。
words.en: Something that is noxious is harmful or poisonous.

words.tr: v. 低声歌唱；低吟；轻哼
words.ex: He likes to croon soft songs at night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在晚上轻声哼唱柔和的歌曲。
words.en: If you croon, you sing or hum quietly and gently, often in a low voice.

words.tr:
v. 切碎；剁碎；装腔作势地小步走
n. 绞碎的肉
words.ex: He minces garlic for the sauce.
words.ex_cn: 他把大蒜剁碎用来做酱。
words.en: To mince means to cut food, especially meat, into very small pieces, or to walk or speak in an affected manner.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.ex: The child threw a tantrum when he couldn't get what he wanted.
words.ex_cn: 孩子因为得不到想要的东西而发脾气。
words.en: A tantrum is an uncontrolled outburst of anger and frustration, typically in a young child.

words.tr: adj. 庞大的；笨拙的；似象一样的
words.ex: The elephantine statue stood in the park.
words.ex_cn: 那座巨大的雕像矗立在公园里。
words.en: If you describe something as elephantine, you mean that you think it is large and awkward.

words.tr: adj. 匆忙的；草率的；急躁的
words.ex: He made a hasty decision and regretted it.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个仓促的决定，后来后悔了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as hasty, you mean that they are acting too quickly, without thinking carefully, often with unwanted results.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: The fish has a sharp barb on its tail.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼的尾巴上有一个尖锐的倒刺。
words.en: A barb is a sharp projection near the end of an arrow, fishhook, or similar object, which is angled away from the main point so as to make extraction difficult. It can also refer to a remark that is meant to hurt someone's feelings.

words.ex: The stench from the trash made me sick.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的臭味让我恶心。
words.en: A strong, very unpleasant smell.

words.ex: The tree has spindly branches reaching toward the sky.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树有细长的枝条伸向天空。
words.en: Something that is spindly is long and thin and looks as if it is weak or easily broken.

words.ex: The ungainly boy tripped over his own feet.
words.ex_cn: 这个笨拙的男孩被自己的脚绊倒了。
words.en: If you describe a person, animal, or vehicle as ungainly, you mean that they look awkward or clumsy, often because they are big.

words.tr: v. 游移不定；踌躇；犹豫
words.ex: He vacillates between choosing tea or coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择茶还是咖啡之间犹豫不决。
words.en: To vacillate means to waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.tr:
n. 大洪水；暴雨；泛滥
v. 泛滥；大量涌入
words.ex: The rain caused a deluge in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨在镇上引发了洪水。
words.en: A deluge is a severe flood or a very heavy fall of rain that causes a lot of damage.

words.tr:
adj. 超自然的；神秘的；隐藏的
v. 掩蔽
n. 神秘的事物；神秘学
words.ex: He is interested in the occult.
words.ex_cn: 他对神秘学感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to mystical, supernatural, or magical powers, practices, or phenomena.

words.ex: He embarrassed himself in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班同学面前让自己丢脸了。
words.en: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel shy, ashamed, or guilty about something.

words.ex: The river water looked murky after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，河水看起来污浊。
words.en: If you describe something as murky, you mean that the details of it are not clear or that it is difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的； v. “compel”的现在分词；
words.ex: His story was compelling and made everyone listen.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事令人信服，让所有人都认真聆听。
words.en: A compelling argument or reason is one that makes you believe it or accept it because it is so strong.

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr:
n. 系绳；系链；界限
v. 用绳拴住
words.ex: The horse was tied to the post with a tether.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马被用拴绳系在了柱子上。
words.en: A tether is a rope or chain used to tie an animal to a post or other fixed point so that it cannot move away.

words.ex: The big company tries to monopolize the market.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司试图垄断市场。
words.en: If a company or person monopolizes something, they have complete control over it, so that other people cannot share it.

words.ex: He told a silly jape to make his friends laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个愚蠢的玩笑来逗朋友们笑。
words.en: A jape is a practical joke or a witty remark.

words.ex: The book uses demotic language to reach ordinary people.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使用通俗的语言来吸引普通人。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the form of a language used by ordinary people; vernacular.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.tr:
v. 献出；拿出；提供
n. 献出；拿出；提供
words.ex: He proffered a cup of tea to his guest.
words.ex_cn: 他递给客人一杯茶。
words.en: If you proffer something to someone, you offer it to them for acceptance.

words.ex: They hallow the old church on Halloween.
words.ex_cn: 他们在万圣节时敬拜那座老教堂。
words.en: To make holy or set apart as holy; to honor as sacred.

words.ex: The sun parched the land.
words.ex_cn: 太阳晒干了土地。
words.en: To make something very dry, especially by exposure to heat.

words.tr: adj. 有...气味的；令人想起...的
words.ex: The garden is redolent of roses.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园弥漫着玫瑰的香气。
words.en: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.tr: n. 阐述者；拥护者；代表者；指数
words.ex: He is the exponent of modern education reform.
words.ex_cn: 他是现代教育改革的阐述者。
words.en: An exponent is someone who supports and explains a particular idea, theory, or system, or a symbol that shows how many times a number is to be multiplied by itself.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.tr: v. 劝慰；使息怒；谋求好感
words.ex: He brought flowers to propitiate his angry wife.
words.ex_cn: 他带了花去劝慰他生气的妻子。
words.en: To propitiate someone means to make them less angry or hostile by doing something to please them.

words.ex: The unexpected news discomposed her.
words.ex_cn: 突如其来的消息使她不安。
words.en: If something discomposes you, it makes you feel anxious or uneasy.

words.ex: The stock price hit its nadir last month.
words.ex_cn: 股票价格上个月跌至最低点。
words.en: The nadir of something is the worst or lowest point that it reaches.

words.tr: adj. 可悲的；令人惋惜的；质量低劣的
words.ex: The situation was lamentable, with many people losing their homes.
words.ex_cn: 情况非常可悲，许多人失去了家园。
words.en: If you describe something as lamentable, you mean that it is very unfortunate or disappointing.

words.ex: He supplicated for mercy.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求宽恕。
words.en: to ask for something in a humble way; to beg earnestly and humbly

words.tr: adj. 面有愠色的；闷闷不乐的；阴沉的
words.ex: He gave a sullen look when his mom asked him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 当妈妈让他打扫房间时，他一脸阴沉。
words.en: Someone who is sullen is bad-tempered and does not speak much.

words.tr:
adj. 周期的；定期的
n. 期刊
words.ex: The plant has a periodical blooming cycle.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物有周期性的开花周期。
words.en: A periodical is a magazine, especially one that is published regularly, or something that happens at regular intervals.

words.ex: He put the bread in the pan.
words.ex_cn: 他把面包放进平底锅里。
words.en: A pan is a round metal container with a long handle, which is used for cooking things in, usually on top of a stove.

words.tr: adj. 不能生育的；贫瘠的；
words.ex: The doctor said the man is sterile.
words.ex_cn: 医生说这个人不能生育。
words.en: Something that is sterile is completely clean and free from bacteria or other microorganisms.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.ex: He didn't flinch when the needle touched his skin.
words.ex_cn: 当针碰到他的皮肤时，他没有退缩。
words.en: If you flinch, you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.

words.tr: adj. 通过经历而变得顽强的；坚毅的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: The hard-bitten soldier never gave up, even in the face of overwhelming odds.
words.ex_cn: 面对压倒性的劣势，这位顽强的士兵也从未放弃。
words.en: If you describe someone as hard-bitten, you mean that they have been through a lot of difficult or unpleasant experiences and are tough as a result.

words.tr: adj. 慵懒的；没精打采的；懒洋洋的
words.ex: He felt lethargic after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you are lethargic, you do not have much energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.ex: I caught a whiff of fresh bread.
words.ex_cn: 我闻到了一点新鲜面包的气味。
words.en: A whiff is a brief, gentle gust of air, or a slight smell of something.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.tr: adj. 厚颜无耻的；公然的；露骨的
words.ex: He told a barefaced lie in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前厚颜无耻地说谎。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as barefaced, you are saying that it is very bold and that they do not care that it is wrong or that people will be shocked by it.

words.ex: His supposition is that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是明天会下雨。
words.en: A supposition is a guess or a theory that you have about something, which may not be true.

words.ex: The government does a census every ten years.
words.ex_cn: 政府每十年进行一次人口普查。
words.en: A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.

words.ex: The wind abrades the rock slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢磨损岩石。
words.en: To scrape or wear away by friction or erosion.

words.ex: He remained impassive when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个坏消息时，他依然面无表情。
words.en: If someone is impassive, they do not show any emotion.

words.ex: The two roads diverge after the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 两条路在桥后分岔。
words.en: If one thing diverges from another similar thing, the first thing becomes different from the second or develops differently from it. You can also say that two things diverge.

words.tr:
v. 放电；放出；
n. 排放；
words.ex: The battery will discharge if left unused for a long time.
words.ex_cn: 如果长时间不使用，电池会放电。
words.en: If someone is discharged from a hospital, prison, or the armed forces, they are officially allowed to leave, or told that they must leave. If something is discharged from inside a place, it comes out.

words.tr:
v. 没精打采地站（或坐、走）；低头垂肩地站（或坐、走）
n. 没精打采的样子
words.ex: He slouches in his chair while watching TV.
words.ex_cn: 他看电视时驼背坐着。
words.en: If someone slouches, they sit or stand with their shoulders and head bent so that they look lazy and tired.

words.ex: The lustrous pearl shone under the light.
words.ex_cn: 这颗有光泽的珍珠在光下闪耀。
words.en: Something that is lustrous shines brightly and gently, often because it is very smooth or clean.

words.tr:
n. 疑虑；怀疑
v. 使疑虑；使担忧；“misgive”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a misgiving about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划感到不安。
words.en: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or anxiety about something that might happen or might have happened.

words.ex: He talked with bravado, but he was scared.
words.ex_cn: 他装出勇敢的样子说话，但他其实很害怕。
words.en: A bold manner or a show of boldness intended to impress or intimidate.

words.tr:
v. （使）生气
n. 发脾气；微怒
words.ex: She got a miff when I forgot her birthday.
words.ex_cn: 我忘记了她的生日，她有点恼火。
words.en: To cause to be annoyed or offended.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.ex: The restaurant serves a famous delicacy called seafood soup.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅供应一道著名的佳肴，叫海鲜汤。
words.en: Delicacy refers to the quality of being delicate, fine, or subtle in appearance, structure, or manner. It can also denote a choice or rare food item.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.ex: The caterpillar metamorphose into a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 毛毛虫变成了蝴蝶。
words.en: To change completely in form or nature.

words.ex: He used subterfuge to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用遁词来避免回答问题。
words.en: Deceit used in order to achieve one's goal.

words.tr: adj. 厌倦的；冷漠的；玩世不恭的
words.ex: She gave a blas shrug when asked about the award.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及奖项时，她冷漠地耸了耸肩。
words.en: If you describe someone as blas, you mean that they are not easily impressed, excited, or worried by things, usually because they have seen or experienced them before.

words.tr:
n. 信号；
v. 用信号通知；
words.ex: The traffic light is a signal to stop.
words.ex_cn: 交通灯是一个停止的信号。
words.en: A signal is a gesture, sound, or action which is intended to give a particular message to the person who sees or hears it.

words.ex: This coupon is valid until next month.
words.ex_cn: 这张优惠券到下个月都有效。
words.en: If something such as a document or agreement is valid, it is legally acceptable or officially recognized.

words.tr: v. 逐步康复；渐愈；复原
words.ex: He is convalescing at home after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后在家休养。
words.en: To convalesce means to recover health and strength gradually after sickness or weakness.

words.ex: The gladiator fought in the ancient arena.
words.ex_cn: 角斗士在古代竞技场中战斗。
words.en: In ancient Rome, a gladiator was a man trained to fight with weapons against other men or wild animals in an arena.

words.tr:
n. 额外费用；附加费
v. 额外索价；附加罚款
words.ex: He paid a surcharge for extra baggage.
words.ex_cn: 他为额外行李支付了附加费。
words.en: An additional charge or payment.

words.ex: He wore an outlandish hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as outlandish, you mean that it is very unusual, strange, or exaggerated.

words.tr: v. 感到极度焦虑；折磨；苦苦思索
words.ex: He agonizes over his decision every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都为自己的决定而痛苦挣扎。
words.en: To agonize over something means to spend a lot of time worrying and being anxious about it.

words.tr: v. 卸货；（使）下船（或飞机，车等）
words.ex: The passengers began to debark as soon as the ship docked.
words.ex_cn: 船一靠岸，乘客们就开始下船。
words.en: To leave a ship or airplane; to disembark.

words.tr: adj. 可渗透的；可渗入的；
words.ex: The soil is permeable, so water passes through easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤是可渗透的，所以水很容易通过。
words.en: If a substance is permeable, it allows liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢或吃力地走
n. 长途跋涉
words.ex: He trudges through the snow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跋涉穿过雪地。
words.en: To walk slowly and with heavy steps, typically because of exhaustion or harsh conditions.

words.tr:
adj. 犁过而未耕种的；休耕的；休闲中的
n. 休耕的田地；闲置；休整
v. 使（翻耕后的土地）休闲
words.ex: The farmer lets the field lie fallow this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年农夫让这块地休耕。
words.en: If land is fallow, it is not planted with crops, in order to improve the quality of the soil.

words.tr:
n. 杂交种；混合物；
adj. 混合的；
words.ex: The corn hybrid grows faster than the old type.
words.ex_cn: 这种玉米杂交种比旧品种长得更快。
words.en: A hybrid is a plant or animal that has been produced from two different types of plant or animal, especially to get better characteristics. It can also refer to something that is a mixture of two different things.

words.ex: He conflates happiness with wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福和财富混为一谈。
words.en: To combine two or more things into one, especially in a way that is confusing or misleading.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.tr: v. 戒绝；弃权；自我克制
words.ex: He abstains from eating sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他戒食糖。
words.en: If you abstain from something, you deliberately do not do it or have it, especially something you like or enjoy which might be considered bad for you.

words.ex: He outwit the opponent with a clever trick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个聪明的计策胜过了对手。
words.en: To outwit someone means to use your intelligence or a clever trick to defeat them or gain an advantage over them.

words.tr: v. 减到最少；使最小化；
words.ex: Try to minimize waste in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 尽量减少厨房里的浪费。
words.en: To minimize something means to reduce it to the smallest possible amount or degree.

words.ex: He was branded a turncoat after switching political parties.
words.ex_cn: 他在更换政党后被贴上了变节者的标签。
words.en: A turncoat is someone who changes their allegiance or loyalty, especially in a way that is considered treacherous or disloyal.

words.tr:
n. 藏物处；隐藏物；
v. 匿藏；
words.ex: The hunters found a cache of food under the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人们在石头下发现了一个食物藏匿处。
words.en: A cache is a hidden store of things such as weapons or a supply of food.

words.ex: The child's petulant behavior was a result of his frustration.
words.ex_cn: 孩子暴躁的行为是因他的沮丧所致。
words.en: If you describe someone as petulant, you mean that they get angry or annoyed in a childish or unreasonable way.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；含糊地说
n. 含糊的话；咕哝
words.ex: He mumbles when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会嘟囔。
words.en: If you mumble, you speak very quietly and not at all clearly with the result that the words are difficult to understand.

words.ex: The jar is airtight, so the food stays fresh.
words.ex_cn: 这个罐子是密封的，所以食物能保持新鲜。
words.en: If something is airtight, it is completely sealed so that no air can get in or out.

words.tr: adj. 保留的； v. 保留；“reserve”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The seats are reserved for students.
words.ex_cn: 这些座位是为学生保留的。
words.en: If something is reserved, it is kept specially for a particular purpose or person.

words.ex: The two cultures are disparate in their traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化在传统上完全不同。
words.en: Things that are disparate are clearly different from each other in quality or type.

words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.ex: Oil helps to lubricate the engine parts.
words.ex_cn: 油有助于润滑发动机部件。
words.en: To apply a substance such as oil or grease to (something) in order to minimize friction and allow smooth movement.

words.ex: He showed apathy toward the news.
words.ex_cn: 他对这则新闻漠不关心。
words.en: Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern about something. It is a state of indifference, or the suppression of emotions such as concern, excitement, motivation, or passion.

words.tr: adj. 不善交际的；不圆滑的；笨拙的
words.ex: He made a gauche comment at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚宴上说了个笨拙的评论。
words.en: If you describe someone as gauche, you mean that they are awkward and uncomfortable in the company of other people, especially because they lack social skills.

words.tr:
v. 胡说；叫嚷；发狂地说
n. 喧闹的宴会；极力赞扬
words.ex: He was raving about ghosts in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中胡说鬼魂的事。
words.en: To talk or write about something with great enthusiasm or admiration; a large party or dance with electronic music, especially one that lasts all night.

words.tr: n. 礼貌得体；适宜的举止
words.ex: He maintained decorum during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间保持了得体的行为。
words.en: Decorum is behavior that is controlled, calm, and polite, especially in formal situations.

words.tr: v. 歪曲；不实报道；曲解
words.ex: He misrepresents the facts to win the debate.
words.ex_cn: 他歪曲事实以赢得辩论。
words.en: To give a false or misleading account of the nature of something.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.ex: He saw a mirage in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 他在沙漠中看到了海市蜃楼。
words.en: An optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions, especially the appearance of a sheet of water in a desert or on a hot road caused by the refraction of light from the sky by heated air.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.tr:
n. 低语声；嘟哝
v. 低语；咕哝；私下抱怨
words.ex: I heard a murmur from the next room.
words.ex_cn: 我听到隔壁房间传来低语声。
words.en: A murmur is a low, indistinct, continuous sound, as of a stream or of voices.

words.tr: adj. 恶臭的；有恶臭的；有臭味的
words.ex: The malodorous garbage was attracting flies.
words.ex_cn: 那堆有恶臭的垃圾招来了苍蝇。
words.en: Having a very unpleasant smell.

words.tr:
n. 英寻（长度单位）
v. 测深；推测；揣摩；搞懂；彻底了解
words.ex: The ship's anchor sank to a depth of ten fathoms.
words.ex_cn: 船的锚沉到了十英寻的深度。
words.en: If you cannot fathom something, you are unable to understand it, although you think carefully about it.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.tr: adj. 不热心的；心思不够的
words.ex: He gave a halfhearted apology and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地道了歉，然后离开了。
words.en: If someone is halfhearted about something, they do it without enthusiasm or energy.

words.tr: adj. 预示的；凶兆的；装腔作势的
words.ex: The dark clouds are a portentous sign of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的预示。
words.en: If someone's way of speaking, writing, or behaving is portentous, they speak, write, or behave more seriously than necessary because they want to impress other people.

words.tr: adj. 放荡的；肆无忌惮的；潇洒的
words.ex: He wore a rakish hat at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上戴了一顶歪斜的帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone as rakish, you mean that they are stylish and confident in a way that is slightly unconventional and possibly a little disreputable.

words.tr:
n. 小块；碎片；废金属；吵架
v. 废弃；取消
adj. 废弃的
words.ex: He picked up a scrap of paper from the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起一张纸片。
words.en: A scrap is a small piece or amount of something, especially one that is left over after the greater part has been used. It can also mean to discard or get rid of something as being no longer useful or necessary.

words.tr: adj. 濒临死亡的；垂死的；
words.ex: The moribund patient stopped breathing.
words.ex_cn: 这位濒临死亡的病人停止了呼吸。
words.en: If you describe something as moribund, you mean that it is in a very bad condition and is not active or successful.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.ex: Cleaning the whole house is a laborious task.
words.ex_cn: 打扫整个房子是一项耗时费力的任务。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as laborious, you mean that it takes a lot of time and effort.

words.tr: n. 游牧民；流浪者；游牧生活；流浪生活
words.ex: The nomad walks with his sheep across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 游牧民带着他的羊群穿越沙漠。
words.en: A nomad is someone who has no permanent home and moves according to the seasons from place to place in search of food, water, and grazing land.

words.tr: adj. 怕痒的；难对付的；棘手的
words.ex: He is ticklish when someone touches his feet.
words.ex_cn: 当别人碰他的脚时，他会觉得痒。
words.en: If someone is ticklish, they are sensitive to being tickled and may laugh or squirm when touched in a certain way. It can also describe a situation that is difficult or delicate to handle.

words.tr: adj. 多结节的；难以解决的；棘手的
words.ex: The old tree had a knotty trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树有一个多结节的树干。
words.en: A knotty problem or issue is very complicated and difficult to solve.

words.tr:
n. 谷壳；糠；揶揄
v. 开玩笑；戏弄
words.ex: The wind blew away the chaff from the wheat.
words.ex_cn: 风吹走了小麦中的糠秕。
words.en: Chaff is the outer covering of the seeds of grain such as wheat, which is separated from the grain before it is used as food.

words.ex: The temporal change of seasons affects our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 季节的时间变化影响我们的日常生活。
words.en: Relating to time as opposed to eternity; relating to worldly life as opposed to spiritual life.

words.tr: n. 伪装；假象；虚伪的表现
words.ex: He was accused of using pretense to gain sympathy.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控利用伪装来博取同情。
words.en: A pretense is an action or way of behaving that is intended to make people believe something that is not true.

words.ex: He made a loutish noise at the dinner table.
words.ex_cn: 他在餐桌上发出了粗鲁的噪音。
words.en: If you describe someone as loutish, you are critical of them because they behave in an impolite or aggressive way.

words.tr: adj. 词藻浮华的；夸大的；做作的
words.ex: He gave a grandiloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language as grandiloquent, you mean that it is extremely formal, elaborate, or exaggerated, and is used to impress people.

words.ex: He persevered despite many failures.
words.ex_cn: 尽管多次失败，他仍然坚持不懈。
words.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

words.ex: The doctor wrote a prescription for medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一张药方。
words.en: A prescription is a written order from a physician for the preparation and administration of a drug or device for a patient.

words.ex: His tone was one of gentle reproof.
words.ex_cn: 他的语气带着温和的责备。
words.en: An expression of blame or disapproval.

words.ex: He is puny and can't lift the box.
words.ex_cn: 他很瘦弱，举不起那个箱子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puny, you mean that they are small and weak.

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.tr: n. 补药；滋补品；奎宁水
words.ex: He drank a tonic to feel better.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一杯滋补剂来感觉好些。
words.en: A tonic is a medicine that makes you feel stronger, healthier, and less tired.

words.ex: The acme of his career was winning the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的顶点是获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: The highest point of achievement or excellence.

words.ex: I want a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 我想要一杯茶。
words.en: If you want something, you feel a desire or a need for it.

words.ex: The chair has a wobble on one leg.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子有一条腿在晃动。
words.en: If something wobbles or if you wobble it, it moves unsteadily from side to side.

words.tr:
adj. 无用的；琐碎的；微不足道的
v. 撒尿；鬼混；游荡；“piddle”的现在分词
words.ex: He is piddling away his time on useless games.
words.ex_cn: 他正在浪费时间玩无用的游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as piddling, you are emphasizing that it is very small or unimportant.

words.ex: He is pessimistic about the future.
words.ex_cn: 他对未来持悲观态度。
words.en: If someone is pessimistic, they expect that bad things will happen in the future or that something will have a bad result.

words.tr: adj. 无菌的；经消毒的；冷漠的
words.ex: The nurse used an aseptic technique to clean the wound.
words.ex_cn: 护士使用无菌技术清洁伤口。
words.en: Free from contamination caused by harmful bacteria, viruses, or other microorganisms; surgically clean or sterile.

words.ex: The factory released an effluvium into the air.
words.ex_cn: 工厂向空气中排放了一种气味。
words.en: An unpleasant or harmful odor, secretion, or discharge.

words.tr: adj. 不稳定的；飘忽不定的；
words.ex: The weather has been erratic this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的天气一直不稳定。
words.en: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves in unexpected directions.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.tr:
adv. 歪地；斜着
adj. 歪斜的
words.ex: The picture was hanging askew on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 那幅画在墙上挂歪了。
words.en: Not in a straight or level position.

words.ex: The evidence warrants a new investigation.
words.ex_cn: 证据使新的调查成为必要。
words.en: If something warrants a particular action, it makes the action seem necessary or appropriate for the circumstances.

words.ex: He tries to protract the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他试图延长会议。
words.en: To protract something means to make it last longer than usual or necessary, often in a way that is annoying or inconvenient.

words.ex: The school's ethos is respect for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校的社會精神特质是尊重每一个人。
words.en: The fundamental character or spirit of a culture; the underlying sentiment that informs the beliefs, customs, or practices of a group or society.

words.tr: adj. 难消化的，使人胀饱的；古板的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The stodgy pudding made him feel full and uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这道难消化的布丁让他感到胀满不适。
words.en: If you describe something as stodgy, you mean that it is dull, boring, and rather formal.

words.ex: The room was decorated with gaudy colors that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间用俗丽的颜色装饰，刺眼。
words.en: If you describe something as gaudy, you mean that it is very brightly coloured and showy, but not in an attractive way.

words.ex: The child clings to his mother's leg.
words.ex_cn: 孩子紧贴着妈妈的腿。
words.en: If you cling to someone or something, you hold onto them tightly.

words.ex: He has a considerable amount of money.
words.ex_cn: 他有相当多的钱。
words.en: Considerable means large in size, amount, or extent.

words.ex: The news roiled the financial markets.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息搅乱了金融市场。
words.en: To make (a liquid) turbid or muddy by stirring up sediment; to disturb or irritate.

words.ex: The view from the hill is panoramic.
words.ex_cn: 从山上望去，景色一览无余。
words.en: A panoramic view or picture is one that shows a wide area of land or sea.

words.ex: The teacher exhorts students to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师敦促学生努力学习。
words.en: To strongly encourage or try to persuade someone to do something.

words.tr: adj. 无定形的；无组织的；
words.ex: The glass is amorphous because it lacks a regular shape.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃是无定形的，因为它没有规则的形状。
words.en: Lacking a clear shape or form; not clearly defined or structured.

words.ex: The monster was just a figment of his imagination.
words.ex_cn: 那个怪物只是他想象出来的。
words.en: A figment is something that someone imagines or invents, often something that is not real.

words.tr: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；吓倒
words.ex: The loud noise did not daunt her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音并没有吓倒她。
words.en: If something daunts you, it makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；激励；督促
n. 戳；刺；催促
words.ex: He prodded the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke or jab someone or something, often with a finger or a pointed object, in order to get their attention or to encourage them to do something.

words.ex: He lives a spartan life with little food and no luxuries.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，食物很少，也没有奢侈品。
words.en: If you describe something as spartan, you mean that it is very simple and not at all luxurious, often because it is intended to be useful or practical rather than attractive.

words.ex: He abandoned his car in the snow.
words.ex_cn: 他把车抛弃在雪地里。
words.en: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave the place, thing, or person permanently or for a long time, especially when you should not do so.

words.tr: v. 使中立；中和；使无效
words.ex: The government tried to neutralize the conflict by talking to both sides.
words.ex_cn: 政府试图通过与双方交谈来使冲突中立化。
words.en: To neutralize something means to stop it from having any effect or to make it ineffective.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.tr: n. 祸根；致命伤；烦扰之源；
words.ex: Smoking is the bane of his health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是他健康的祸根。
words.en: Something that causes misery or death.

words.ex: The experiment demonstrates that water boils at 100°C.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验证明水在100摄氏度时沸腾。
words.en: To demonstrate means to show something clearly by giving proof or evidence.

words.ex: Mom reassured me that everything would be fine.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈让我安心，一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you reassure someone, you comfort them and stop them from worrying.

words.ex: He was obsessed with the minutiae of daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他对日常生活的琐事着迷。
words.en: The small, precise, or trivial details of something.

words.tr: v. 使慌张；使窘迫；使不安
words.ex: The sudden noise disconcerted her.
words.ex_cn: 突然的噪音让她感到不安。
words.en: If something disconcerts you, it makes you feel anxious, confused, or embarrassed.

words.tr:
adj. 军事的；军用的；
n. 军队；武装力量；
words.ex: The military base is near the border.
words.ex_cn: 军事基地靠近边境。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of soldiers or armed forces

words.ex: He is versed in computer programming.
words.ex_cn: 他精通计算机编程。
words.en: If someone is versed in a particular subject, they know a lot about it.

words.ex: He felt enmity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对他邻居怀有敌意。
words.en: Enmity is a feeling of hostility or ill will towards someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 貌似真实的; 可能的
words.ex: The story she told sounded verisimilar, but we later found out it was fabricated.
words.ex_cn: 她讲述的故事听起来很真实，但我们后来发现它是捏造的。
words.en: Having the appearance of truth; probable or likely.

words.tr: n. 沉重行走的人；慢条斯理的人
words.ex: He is a plodder who works slowly but never gives up.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个缓慢工作但从不放弃的人。
words.en: A plodder is someone who works slowly and steadily, especially in a way that is not very exciting or imaginative but is determined and persistent.

words.ex: He exults when his team wins the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的球队赢得比赛时，他欢呼雀跃。
words.en: If you exult in a triumph or success that you have had, you feel and show great happiness and pride because of it.

words.tr:
v. （声音）颤抖
n. 颤抖的声音
words.ex: His voice quavers when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他的声音会颤抖。
words.en: If someone's voice quavers, it is unsteady because the person is uncertain, nervous, or upset.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: The epilogue showed what happened to the characters after the story ended.
words.ex_cn: 尾声展示了故事结束后角色们的命运。
words.en: An epilogue is a section or speech at the end of a book or play that serves as a comment on or a conclusion to what has happened.

words.ex: He was beset by problems at work.
words.ex_cn: 他被工作中的问题困扰。
words.en: If someone or something is beset by problems or fears, they have many problems or fears which affect them severely.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.ex: He is irascible when he wakes up late.
words.ex_cn: 他起床晚时容易发怒。
words.en: If you describe someone as irascible, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.ex: The email was bogus and tried to steal my password.
words.ex_cn: 这封邮件是假的，试图窃取我的密码。
words.en: If you describe something as bogus, you mean that it is not genuine, true, or real.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr: adj. 倾向性的；有偏见的；有争议的
words.ex: The media's tendentious reporting often misrepresents the truth.
words.ex_cn: 媒体的带有倾向性的报道常常歪曲事实。
words.en: If something is tendentious, it expresses a particular opinion or point of view very strongly, especially one that many people disagree with.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The child was compliant and followed all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子很顺从，遵守了所有规则。
words.en: If someone or something is compliant, they act in accordance with rules, standards, or laws.

words.tr:
v. 啄；连续敲击；轻吻
n. 啄痕；啄食；轻吻
words.ex: The bird pecked at the bread on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿啄地上的面包。
words.en: To peck means to strike or bite something with the beak, or to kiss someone lightly and quickly.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.tr:
n. 说笑；玩笑
v. 开玩笑
words.ex: He likes to jest with his friends during lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在午餐时和朋友开玩笑。
words.en: A jest is a remark that is intended to be amusing or funny, especially one that is made in a light-hearted or teasing manner.

words.ex: The teacher will not condone cheating in exams.
words.ex_cn: 老师不会容忍考试作弊。
words.en: To condone something means to accept or allow behavior that is considered wrong.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.ex: I loathe waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: If you loathe something or someone, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: The mother sang a lullaby to her baby.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈为她的宝宝唱了一首摇篮曲。
words.en: A lullaby is a quiet song which is intended to be sung to babies and young children to help them go to sleep.

words.ex: The rapscallion stole an apple from the market.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽童从市场偷了一个苹果。
words.en: A rapscallion is someone who behaves badly, often in a playful or mischievous way.

words.tr: n. 骚动；骚乱；心烦意乱
words.ex: The crowd caused a tumult after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，人群引起了混乱。
words.en: A tumult is a state of confusion, noise, and excitement, often involving a large group of people.

words.ex: The teacher tried to infuse confidence into the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师试图向学生注入信心。
words.en: If you infuse a quality into someone or something, you fill them with it. If a quality infuses something, it is present throughout it.

words.ex: The rickety table wobbled when I put my book on it.
words.ex_cn: 这张不结实的桌子当我把书放上去时晃动了。
words.en: Likely to fall or collapse; shaky.

words.tr: adj. 可延展的；易于塑造的
words.ex: The gold is ductile and can be drawn into thin wires.
words.ex_cn: 金具有延展性，可以拉成细丝。
words.en: A ductile material is one that can be stretched into a wire or hammered into a thin sheet without breaking.

words.ex: The soldiers reconnoiter the enemy's position before attacking.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在进攻前侦察敌人的阵地。
words.en: To reconnoiter means to make a military observation of a region to locate an enemy or ascertain strategic features.

words.ex: The imperious queen demanded immediate obedience.
words.ex_cn: 这位专横的女王要求立即服从。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperious, you mean that they have a proud manner and expect to be obeyed.

words.ex: The rope is slack and hangs loosely.
words.ex_cn: 绳子是松弛的，垂挂着。
words.en: If something is slack, it is loose and not firmly stretched or tightly in position. It can also describe a period of low activity or a lack of effort in work or activity.

words.tr: v. （使）分成两叉；（使）分成两支
words.ex: The river bifurcates into two smaller streams.
words.ex_cn: 这条河分岔成两条小溪。
words.en: To bifurcate means to divide or fork into two branches or parts.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.tr: v. 笨拙地弄糟；笨手笨脚地走动；语无伦次
words.ex: He bumbled the presentation and forgot his lines.
words.ex_cn: 他笨拙地搞砸了演讲，忘记了台词。
words.en: To bumble is to move or act in an awkward or confused manner, often making mistakes or being inefficient.

words.ex: The children stood in awe at the sight of the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到山时感到敬畏。
words.en: A feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；肤浅的；易做到的
words.ex: He gave a facile answer to the hard question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个简单的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's arguments or suggestions as facile, you are criticizing them because their ideas are too simple and indicate a lack of careful, intelligent thinking.

words.ex: Her strident voice broke the silence.
words.ex_cn: 她尖锐的声音打破了寂静。
words.en: If you use strident to describe someone or the way they express themselves, you mean that they make their feelings or opinions known in a very strong way that perhaps makes people uncomfortable.

words.ex: The floor has a colorful mosaic of flowers.
words.ex_cn: 地板上有一个五彩的花卉镶嵌图案。
words.en: A mosaic is a picture or pattern produced by arranging together small colored pieces of hard material, such as stone, tile, or glass.

words.ex: He is a man of great wit.
words.ex_cn: 他是个极具机智的人。
words.en: Wit is the ability to use words or ideas in a quick, clever, and amusing way.

words.ex: The teacher gave us the syllabus for the course.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我们这门课的教学大纲。
words.en: A syllabus is an outline or summary of the main points of a text, lecture, or course of study.

words.tr: v. 故态复萌；退步；再犯
words.ex: He backslid into old habits after quitting smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他戒烟后又回到了旧习惯。
words.en: To revert to bad habits or undesirable activities after a period of improvement.

words.ex: His efforts were bootless.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力是徒劳的。
words.en: If you describe something as bootless, you mean that it is useless or does not achieve anything.

words.ex: The company agreed to defray the travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司同意支付差旅费。
words.en: If you defray someone's costs or expenses, you give them money which represents the amount that they have spent, for example while they have been doing something for you or acting on your behalf.

words.tr:
v. 挡开；避开；回避
n. 挡开；闪避
words.ex: He parries the punch with his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他用胳膊格挡了这一拳。
words.en: If you parry a question or argument, you cleverly avoid answering it or dealing with it. In fencing, if you parry a blow, you defend yourself against it by pushing it away with your weapon.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.ex: Happy is synonymous with joyful.
words.ex_cn: 快乐与喜悦是同义的。
words.en: If you say that one thing is synonymous with another, you mean that the two things are very closely associated with each other so that one suggests the other or one cannot exist without the other.

words.tr: n. 听力所及的范围；可听距离
words.ex: Keep your voice down; I don't want anyone within earshot to hear our conversation.
words.ex_cn: 小声点；我不想让听力所及范围内的任何人听到我们的谈话。
words.en: The range within which one can hear or be heard.

words.ex: He was ravenous after running five miles.
words.ex_cn: 跑了五英里后，他饿极了。
words.en: If you are ravenous, you are extremely hungry.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.ex: He adapted to the new school quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就适应了新学校。
words.en: To make suitable to or fit for a specific use or situation.

words.tr: adj. 引人注意的； v. “arrest”的现在分词；
words.ex: She wore an arresting red dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件引人注目的红色连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: If something is arresting, it is very attractive or striking in a way that draws your attention.

words.tr: adj. 震耳欲聋的；极响的
words.ex: The earsplitting noise woke me up.
words.ex_cn: 那刺耳的噪音把我吵醒了。
words.en: An earsplitting noise is extremely loud and unpleasant.
